title: Mental Imagery and Cognitive Function: A Theory-Driven Systematic Review of Behavioral Outcomes and Neuroplastic Mechanisms Across Clinical and Healthy Populations.
abstract: Cognitive decline is a growing concern across the lifespan, impacting quality of life and functional independence. While imagery-based interventions have shown promise for enhancing cognitive function, the strength of evidence, neurobiological mechanisms, and optimal protocols remain unclear. This systematic review synthesized behavioral and neurobiological evidence on imagery-based interventions for cognitive enhancement across healthy and clinical populations, using a theory-driven framework integrating Kosslyn's Theory and Dual-Coding Theory. A comprehensive search was conducted in six major databases (Web of Science, PubMed, Scopus, EBSCO, ScienceDirect, and ProQuest) for studies published up to March 2025. Eligible studies included English-language experimental research on imagery interventions targeting cognitive outcomes. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with dual independent screening, risk of bias assessment (RoB 2/ROBINS-I), and structured data extraction. Effect sizes were synthesized, and subgroup analyses explored moderators such as population type, intervention modality, and duration. Twelve experimental studies (n = 400) met inclusion criteria, encompassing diverse populations. Imagery interventions yielded consistent improvements in cognitive performance, reflected in faster reaction times, higher accuracy, and better task-switching efficiency across both healthy and clinical populations. Gains were most evident in executive control and working memory, accompanied by enhanced activation within prefrontal-parietal networks and increased cortical synchronization, indicating neuroplastic adaptation. Longer intervention duration (> 6 weeks) produced more stable cognitive benefits, whereas evidence on long-term retention remains limited. Although imagery interventions show promise, methodological heterogeneity, limited sample sizes, and short follow-up periods constrain generalizability. Structured motor imagery may enhance cognitive function, potentially via neuroplastic mechanisms. Future research should emphasize large-scale, biomarker-informed RCTs with standardized protocols and inclusive sampling.

title: Glutamatergic Neural and Muscular Systems in Ctenophores.
abstract: Despite glutamate's widespread role as the dominant excitatory transmitter in vertebrate brains, the early evolution of glutamate and its recruitment into neural signaling remain largely unknown. The major limitation is the lack of information on its distribution in early-branching basal metazoans, such as ctenophores (comb jellies). Here, using glutamate immunoreactivity (IR) in two ctenophore species with distinct ecologies (Pleurobrachia bachei and Beroe abyssicola), we show that glutamate IR marks neuronal subpopulations within the subepithelial neural network and small groups of mesogleal neuron-like cells and that it differentially labels some muscle fibers. Remarkably, we also observed an enriched glutamate-ir signal within the nuclei of subepithelial neurons in Beroe. However, glutamate expression levels are species-specific, suggesting tight coupling between glutamate recruitment for neural communication and energetic demands.

title: Tissue and Cerebral Biofluid Remodelling of tRNA-Derived Small RNA Signatures in Experimental and Human Epilepsy.
abstract: Small noncoding RNAs are increasingly recognized as important regulators of gene expression in brain diseases including epilepsy. tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) including tRNA fragments (tRFs) and tRNA halves (tiRNAs) are emerging as stable and regulated RNA species which respond to cellular stress and accumulate in disease states. Using experimental temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) models and human TLE samples, we here determine whether tsRNAs are localized to specific tissue and biofluid compartments in the brain and how they are altered in epilepsy. We analysed small RNA sequencing datasets from hippocampal tissue, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and hippocampal interstitial fluid over time from rat TLE models, and human CSF from control subjects and TLE patients. Small RNA class composition, tsRNA subclass distributions, parent tRNA origins, and differential tsRNA expression profiles were systematically compared across intracellular and extracellular compartments, experimental epilepsy models, and human TLE samples. All differential expression analyses applied Benjamini-Hochberg correction. This revealed that small RNA composition varied strongly by compartment. Hippocampal tissue was dominated by microRNAs, while CSF and interstitial fluid contained significant proportions of tRNA-derived reads. In chronic epilepsy, hippocampal tissue showed a significant increase in overall tsRNA content and in the proportion of tRNA-derived reads, without a significant shift in tsRNA class composition. The CSF and interstitial fluid of epileptic animals showed fragment-level remodelling of tsRNA profiles, although compositional shifts did not reach significance after correction. The CSF from TLE patients also showed extracellular tsRNA populations with potential disease-associated shifts in small RNA composition. Fragments derived from parent tRNAs GlyGCC and GluCTC were recurrent contributors across compartments, though their prominence was compartment-dependent. Collectively, these findings suggest that tsRNAs represent a prominent, compartment-specific, and disease-associated layer of small RNA remodelling in experimental and human epilepsy. The findings may guide the choice of biofluid source and panel of RNAs for biomarker-based diagnostics or provide targets for new therapeutic approaches in drug-resistant epilepsies.

title: Ten myths about milrinone in pediatric cardiogenic shock.
abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a severe and increasingly common condition in children, representing a global health and economic burden. Inodilators (i.e., vasoactive agents with inotropic and vasodilator effects), most commonly dobutamine and milrinone, are the cornerstone of pharmacological treatment for CS in children. Although pediatric guidelines still recommend dobutamine as the first-line inodilator in CS, the use of milrinone has become predominant in this indication. Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase - 3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects and is commonly regarded as offering several theoretical advantages over dobutamine. Based on a critical review of current evidence, we examine here ten myths about milrinone in pediatric CS. The hemodynamic profile of milrinone in CS appears to rely primarily on vasodilation, with limited evidence for clinically meaningful inotropic or lusitropic effects. Current data support a neutral effect on myocardial oxygen consumption and an efficacy in preventing low cardiac output syndrome after pediatric cardiac surgery, while milrinone clearance is reduced in acute kidney injury with unclear clinical significance. However, no consistent evidence demonstrates milrinone's superiority over dobutamine in reducing mortality, length of hospital stay, or tachyarrhythmia, nor its greater efficacy in patients receiving beta-blockers. Its presumed benefits in newborns and in patients with right ventricular failure or pulmonary hypertension remain uncertain and warrant further investigation. What is known: • Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects. • Milrinone has become the preferred inodilator over dobutamine in pediatric cardiogenic shock. What is new: • Milrinone's efficacy appears to stem from vasodilation rather than significant inotropy or lusitropy. • No consistent evidence shows its superiority over dobutamine; further study is warranted.

title: Author Correction: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers.
Human nasal epithelial cells as an integrated platform for biomarker discovery, functional airway studies, and patient-specific stem cell generation.
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
abstract: Studying epithelial dysfunction in respiratory diseases requires physiologically relevant human models that faithfully recapitulate airway structure and function. Primary human nasal epithelial cells (hNECs) represent an accessible and clinically validated system, widely used for mutation-specific drug theratyping. However, the broader potential of hNECs as an integrated experimental platform remains underexplored. Here, we establish a customized hNEC-based platform spanning ex vivo, in vitro, and stem cell-based applications, with direct relevance to precision medicine. Using freshly fixed nasal brushings, we developed a quantitative single-cell metric to assess Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) localization at the ionocyte plasma membrane, identifying a candidate ex vivo biomarker sensitive to disease status and pharmacological modulation in cystic fibrosis (CF). In parallel, transcriptomic profiling demonstrated that air-liquid interface-differentiated hNECs closely recapitulate the molecular features of native nasal epithelium. Functionally, differentiated hNECs reproduced key properties of airway surface liquid (ASL) physiology and its dysregulation under inflammatory and CF conditions. Finally, we show that basal hNECs provide a robust and accessible source for induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) generation. hNEC-derived iPSCs exhibited canonical pluripotency features, differentiated efficiently into germ layer derivatives and lung progenitors, and displayed transcriptomic profiles indistinguishable from iPSCs generated from other somatic sources, supporting their suitability for patient-specific disease modeling. Collectively, these findings position hNECs as an integrated, patient-specific platform linking ex vivo biomarker discovery, in vitro functional assays, and stem cell-based modeling, thereby expanding their utility for precision medicine.

title: Sore throat? The brain has surprising control over how ill you feel.
A scalable subject-specific manifold learning framework for neuroimaging data.
abstract: Low-dimensional manifolds underlie mental and cognitive representations, and characterizing individual differences is critical to neuropsychiatric research. Existing manifold learning methods either distort subject-specific features through population-level alignment or limit cross-subject comparisons with individualized models. We introduce a scalable, subject-specific manifold learning framework with two modules: one capturing individual spatial variation via individualized spatial weights, and an efficient variant reducing computational cost with minimal performance loss. Simulations show that population-level alignment distorts manifold geometry, whereas our approach preserves subject-specific structure. Applied to movie-watching fMRI, our modules improve behavioral label recovery and reconstruction accuracy. In clinical resting-state fMRI, the efficient module identifies individualized spatial activation patterns highlighting sensorimotor, learning, and emotion-related regions. Further validation on an independent resting-state dataset demonstrates 95% test-retest identification accuracy. Together, these results show our framework is robust, reproducible, and broadly applicable across computational neuroscience and clinical research.

title: Shared and distinct neural pathways of aversive and appetitive pain-related learning.
abstract: Aversive and appetitive learning are central to adaptive behaviour, and pain and avoidance are powerful examples of such forces shaping human behaviour. Alterations in learning are thought to contribute to the development and maintenance of chronic pain, yet their neural underpinnings remain unclear. In this registered within-subject fMRI study (German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS-ID: DRKS00027448), we examined both aversive and appetitive pain learning during acquisition and extinction in 68 healthy individuals. Ratings confirm successful learning, with exploratory analyses suggesting stronger aversive acquisition and incomplete extinction. Both conditions engage the visual cortex during acquisition, with increased connectivity to the right operculum. Aversive acquisition further elicits stronger mediodorsal thalamus activity and heightened connectivity with the locus coeruleus, alongside sustained parahippocampal activation during extinction. Incomplete aversive extinction is linked to ongoing visual cortex activity during pain anticipation. Findings suggest shared neural substrates, but stronger aversive recruitment of rapid encoding and persistent memory systems.

title: An engineered nanobody inhibitor for molecular-to-circuit control of opioid receptors.
abstract: Opioid receptors (ORs) orchestrate pain relief, reward and dependence, yet their signaling across diverse cell types and subcellular compartments cannot be resolved by current pharmacological or genetic approaches. Single-domain antibodies, or nanobodies (Nbs), can probe receptor states, but their potential for controlling native receptor signaling at the systems level remains unexplored. Here we engineer high-affinity intracellular Nbs that bind active ORs through structure-guided evolution. Iterative functional optimization yields Nb64, an active-state-selective inhibitor that rapidly suppresses transducer engagement, receptor internalization and downstream signaling, including native μOR-driven G protein-coupled inwardly rectifying potassium currents in ventral tegmental area neurons. Organelle targeting enables precise subcellular control of OR signaling, while bioreversible cell-penetrating peptide conjugation enables nongenetic cytosolic delivery. Cell-type-specific Nb64 expression in ventral tegmental area GABAergic neurons attenuates fentanyl-evoked dopamine release and behavioral responses in mice. Nb64 provides a versatile strategy for dissecting OR biology and establishes a generalizable framework for precision inhibition of native G protein-coupled-receptor signaling in vivo.

title: Brain extracellular matrix remodelling in health and neuropsychiatric disorders.
abstract: The neural extracellular matrix (ECM) is increasingly recognized as an active regulator of brain function and an important contributor to the pathogenesis of neuropsychiatric disorders. This Review examines ECM organization, function and adaptive remodelling in the healthy brain and synthesizes evidence for its pathophysiological alterations in schizophrenia, major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder. Based on findings from human studies and animal models, we propose an ECM-extended conceptual framework of major psychiatric diseases in which polygenic liability, stress exposure and neuroinflammatory signalling converge to remodel the ECM in circuits supporting reward processing, emotion regulation, cognitive control and social cognition. In this model, an early phase of protease-dominant ECM loosening destabilizes microcircuits composed of parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory neurons and principal cells whereas later reactive ECM rebuilding stabilizes dysfunctional network states and contributes to disease persistence, relapse and treatment resistance. This framework positions the ECM as a central hub of genetic, glial, synaptic and systems-level pathogenesis and suggests avenues for the development of ECM-sensitive biomarkers and ECM-directed interventions that may improve the treatment of these disorders.

title: Psilocybin reproducibility.
Leveraging large language models to map triggers of contamination-related obsessive-compulsive symptoms.
abstract: Recent advancements in natural language processing and large language models (LLMs) facilitate the study of under-researched areas in mental health. Their capacity to automatically and meaningfully analyze large-scale text data makes them particularly valuable for studying highly individualized phenomena with clinical relevance, such as triggers of obsessive-compulsive symptoms (OCS), where pattern identification is often challenging. To address this gap, we surveyed 1495 individuals from the general population about contamination-related obsessive-compulsive symptoms (C-OCS), as well as their triggers and corresponding intensity. Using LLM-based embeddings, we generated a map of key trigger categories for C-OCS, revealing their diversity across ecological domains and varying degrees of semantic similarity. Monte Carlo simulations further showed that individuals frequently reported semantically similar trigger pairs that differed in intensity. These findings provide a basis for further investigations into associative learning processes at the categorical and semantic levels, which may enhance understanding of mechanisms involved in the development, maintenance and treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorders.

title: Factors associated with transmission of Mediterranean diet from mothers to children and maintaining it during childhood in the mother-child INMA cohort study.
abstract: The Mediterranean diet (MD) promotes metabolic health and development, but evidence on its intergenerational transmission remains limited. This study aimed to assess the association between maternal adherence to the MD during pregnancy and offspring MD adherence at 4 and 8 years, and to identify sociodemographic and lifestyle-associated factors of its maintenance. We conducted cross-sectional analyses of 1770 mother-child pairs at 4 years and 1497 at 8 years within the INfancia y Medio Ambiente (INMA) mother-child cohort study. Maternal and child Mediterranean diet adherence at ages 4 and 8 years was assessed using validated food frequency questionnaires and then used to calculate the relative Mediterranean diet score (0-16). Adherence was categorized as low (0-6), intermediate (7-10), or high (11-16), and as non-adherent (0-6) or adherent (7-16). Children were classified into four categories according to their maintenance of adherence between 4 and 8 years as adherence, loss of adherence, improved adherence, and no adherence. Linear, logistic, and multinomial regression models were applied to estimate adjusted regressions coefficients (ß), odds ratios (OR), and relative risks ratios (RRR), respectively, and their 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). Children of adherent mothers (7-16 points) had higher odds of being adherent at 4 years (OR = 1.72; 95% CI 1.36-2.18), and at 8 years (OR = 1.73; 95% CI 1.33-2.26). Children of mothers with high adherence (score 11-16) showed higher adherence at 4 (RRR = 4.69; 95% CI 2.90-7.59) and at 8 years (RRR = 2.05; 95% CI 1.22-3.43). The maintenance of child MD adherence from 4 to 8 years was positively associated with maternal adherence and educational level, and negatively with higher television viewing time. This study shows that higher maternal adherence to the MD during pregnancy was associated with higher MD adherence in offspring at ages 4 and 8 years, although more studies should confirm these results and the role of other factors. • The Mediterranean diet has been linked to health benefits and child development. • Family environment is key to consolidating healthy dietary habits in childhood that persist over time, but evidence the intergenerational transmission of the Mediterranean diet from mother to off spring remains limited. • Higher maternal Mediterranean diet adherence during pregnancy was associated with higher off spring adherence at 4 and 8 years. • Maintenance of the child's adherence to the Mediterranean diet between 4 and 8 years was positively associated with maternal adherence and educational level, and negatively with higher television viewing.

title: Foot-focused sexual interest without self-reported distress or interference: associations with male sexual function in a single-center cross-sectional study.
abstract: Clinical evidence on the relationship between foot-focused sexual interest and male sexual function remains limited. We investigated whether current foot-focused sexual interest without self-reported distress or interference was associated with sexual function in men attending a general urology outpatient clinic. This single-center cross-sectional study included 283 participants, 85 with and 198 without current foot-focused sexual interest. Exposure was classified using a study-specific, non-diagnostic questionnaire. The primary endpoint was the functional score of the Male Sexual Health Questionnaire-Ejaculatory Dysfunction Short Form; secondary endpoints were the five-item International Index of Erectile Function and self-estimated intravaginal ejaculation latency time. The exposed group had a lower mean ejaculatory functional score than the unexposed group (12.1 ± 2.2 versus 12.9 ± 1.9; P = 0.009). After adjustment, exposure was associated with a 0.72-point lower score (95% confidence interval, -1.23 to -0.20; P = 0.007). This difference was small and of uncertain clinical relevance. No clear associations were observed with erectile function, self-estimated intravaginal ejaculation latency time, or ejaculatory bother.

title: Scalable electron tomography for connectomics.
abstract: We demonstrate limited-tilt, serial-section electron tomography (ET), which can non-destructively map brain circuits over large 3D volumes and provide high-resolution, supramolecular details within subvolumes of interest. Here we show accelerated ET imaging of semi-thick sections ( >500 nm) from the mouse cerebellar cortex, with 3D resolution <15 nm and machine learning-based image augmentation, providing the capacity to resolve key features of neuronal circuits including chemical synapses, endocytic structures and gap junctions. Furthermore, we systematically assess how imaging parameters affect image quality and speed to enable connectomic-scale projects.

title: GBA1 mutations as a role model for precision medicine in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Genetic variants in GBA1, encoding the lysosomal enzyme glucocerebrosidase (GCase), represent the strongest genetic risk factor for Parkinson's disease (PD) and provide a mechanistic link between Gaucher disease (GD) and PD. While biallelic GBA1 mutations cause GD, heterozygous variants confer an increased, age-dependent risk of PD, with mutation-specific differences in penetrance, age at onset, cognitive decline, and survival. This review critically examines the molecular and clinical spectrum of GBA1-associated PD (GBA1-PD), highlighting the relationship between variant severity, lysosomal dysfunction, and disease progression. We discuss two major, partially overlapping pathogenic frameworks underlying GBA1-PD: loss-of-function mechanisms associated with reduced GCase activity, glycosphingolipid accumulation, and impaired autophagy-lysosomal pathways, and toxic gain-of-function mechanisms driven by mutant GCase misfolding, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and proteostatic imbalance. Increasing evidence suggests that these mechanisms converge on α-synuclein aggregation and dopaminergic neurodegeneration. We further summarize emerging disease-modifying therapeutic strategies, including small-molecule GCase activators, pharmacological chaperones, substrate reduction therapies, acid ceramidase inhibitors, and gene therapies. Although clinical outcomes have been heterogeneous, GBA1-associated PD represents a valuable model for precision medicine, illustrating how genetic stratification can guide mechanism-based therapeutic development in neurodegeneration.

title: Insulin-independent glucose uptake into mouse skeletal muscle by a sodium/glucose linked transporter.
abstract: Exercise is a cornerstone therapy for diabetes because working skeletal muscles take up glucose at dramatically greater rates than postprandial uptake and, notably, do so without a requirement for insulin. Insulin-independent glucose uptake operates normally during exercise and other conditions when adrenergic stimulation inhibits pancreatic insulin release, and it provides a means of glucose disposal in insulin resistant conditions. However, the mechanisms of insulin-independent glucose uptake are not fully understood. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized glucose uptake pathway in muscle, which we refer to as mSGLT based on shared properties with the sodium/glucose cotransporter family (SGLT/Slc5a). In contrast to the abundant muscle GLUT4 transporter, mSGLT activity is not regulated by insulin, requires Na,K-ATPase-α2 activity, and transports the hexose α-methyl-D-glucoside (αMDG), a glucose derivative that is handled by SGLTs but not GLUT4. mSGLT shares antigenicity with the kidney SGLT2 and localizes to the muscle t-tubules together with Na,K-ATPase-α2 and MAP17, the regulatory subunit of SGLT2. Skeletal muscles do not express a full-length transcript of Slc5a2, and mSGLT shows weak affinity for SGLT2-specific inhibitors. mSGLT may be a muscle SGLT isoform. mSGLT and its regulation offer potential muscle-specific targets for treating hyperglycemia and conditions when insulin-stimulated glucose disposal into muscle is impaired.

title: A state-dependent glymphatic dimension in major depressive disorder: implications for treatment resistance.
abstract: The glymphatic system refers to cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange and proposed drainage pathways shaped by sleep, arousal, vascular dynamics, and astrocytic organization. This physiology offers a way to connect disturbances that often coexist in major depressive disorder (MDD): disrupted sleep, fatigue, cognitive slowing, and stress-related abnormalities. We propose that difficulty establishing or maintaining a coordinated sleep-astrocyte-vascular state may contribute to illness persistence in some patients. Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) provides a setting in which this possibility can be examined across the course of treatment. Preclinical studies link stress and depressive-like behavior to astrocytic injury, aquaporin-4 dysregulation, and altered fluid transport. Human imaging findings vary across depressive phenotypes. In a dedicated TRD study, a higher diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) ratio was partly driven by reduced denominator diffusivity, illustrating the importance of interpreting this indirect index at component level. Whole-brain spatiotemporal models provide a complementary account of the neural activity accompanying these physiological states. Ketamine/esketamine, transcranial magnetic stimulation, and chronobiological interventions offer different ways to investigate treatment-related change; serotonergic psychedelics provide an exploratory extension. Longitudinal studies can establish how changes in sleep, fluid-sensitive imaging, and neural dynamics relate temporally to clinical recovery. This Perspective therefore develops a potentially modifiable physiological dimension of persistent depressive illness and defines how it can be tested.

title: AP-1-IL-1β signaling pathway on impulsive-like behavior and memory deficits in aged mice under tibial plateau fracture conditions.
abstract: Tibial fracture surgery has attracted significant interest as a notable trigger for PND. Under external stimuli such as anesthesia and surgery, the transcription factor AP-1 regulates the abnormal expression of glutamatergic neurons via interleukin-1β (IL-1β), a mechanism closely related to the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases. Our research found that anesthesia and surgical exposure increased the time spent in the open arm and decreased the freezing time during context-related fear conditioning in aged mice. These effects were associated with an increase in AP-1-specific expression and elevated levels of inflammatory cytokines in glutamatergic neurons. T-5224, an inhibitor of AP-1, significantly ameliorated tibial plateau fracture (TF)-induced behavioral and memory impairment, suppressed AP-1 levels in glutamatergic neurons, reduced IL-1β expression, attenuated microglial overactivation and synaptic over-pruning, and restored neuronal structure and synaptic morphology in the hippocampus. These findings reveal that anesthesia and surgery induce impulsive-like behaviors and memory impairments in aged mice, which may be associated with inflammatory responses and synaptic loss triggered by activation of the AP-1-IL-1β pathway and overexpression of excitatory neurons in the hippocampus.

title: Predicting Alzheimer progression using EEG-based digital twins.
abstract: Early and accurate prognosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains limited by current biomarkers, which are often invasive, require expensive equipment, or fail to predict individual trajectories of cognitive decline. In this study, we evaluated the Digital Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis (DADD) model, a digital twin framework that extracts neurodegeneration-related digital biomarkers from non-invasive recordings such as electroencephalography (EEG), mapping early functional neural alterations to latent parameters linked to structural AD mechanisms. DADD was applied to a cohort of 459 participants with Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD) or Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), evaluating its performance against established AD biomarkers like APOE genotype, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) markers in predicting prognostic outcomes over a 10-year follow-up. Digital biomarkers demonstrated strong prognostic value, predicting participants who converted at follow-up, significantly outperforming standard EEG metrics. They also robustly forecast both risk and timing of clinical conversion, matching the performance of established AD biomarkers and even outperforming them in SCD participants. Moreover, combining established AD biomarkers with digital biomarkers led to a significant increase in prognostic accuracy. DADD represents a robust clinical tool, enabling scalable, affordable, non-invasive AD detection and prognostic stratification across diverse clinical settings.

title: Dosage compensation is regulated by segregated chromatin modules during development in Drosophila.
abstract: Dosage compensation (DC) restores the expression balance between the X chromosome and autosomes in males. How this chromosome-wide regulation is precisely regulated to accommodate the heterogeneous functions and dosage-sensitivity among X-linked genes is unclear. To address this, we analyse the epigenomic and 3D genome data of mostly sexed samples from embryos to adults of Drosophila melanogaster, whose DC is known to be mediated by three classes of X-enriched sequence elements of HAS/CES, PionX and 1.6883F satellites. We find that about 30% of the X-linked genes are compensated specifically in one or a few male stages or tissues, indicated by their significant bindings of the DC-associated protein or H4K16ac histone modification. These specifically (SDC) or facultatively (FDC) compensated genes are more likely to have a developmentally regulated expression and a highly relevant function with the stage or tissue where they are compensated. They show a higher level of co-binding of facultative heterochromatin hallmark H3K27me3 than the constitutively (CDC) compensated housekeeping genes. CDC genes preferentially harbor constitutive long-range (>1Mb) contacts (LRCs) with other CDC genes and the HAS elements, which form by the onset of DC in embryos. While SDC and FDC genes show developmentally increased LRCs with the respective type of genes and the PionX elements and 1.6883F satellites. The CDC genes and their interacting partners more often coincide with the constitutive boundaries of topologically associated domains, while the other DC genes tend to coincide with the developmentally regulated boundaries. Our results uncover that the Drosophila DC is regulated through separate chromatin modules between housekeeping vs. developmental genes involving different combinations of regulatory sequence elements and 3D genome contacts. This provides broad implications for the hierarchical regulation of DC against different developmental and gene backgrounds among other organisms.

title: Polygenic risk-informed white matter integrity improves deep learning-based prediction of youth depression.
abstract: Early detection of youth depression is crucial, given its rising prevalence and long-term consequences. Although genetic factors contribute significantly to youth depression, their integration with neuroimaging remains limited. This study aims to bridge the gap by predicting youth depression through a combined genetic and neuroimaging framework. We present a deep learning framework using polygenic risk scores to pretrain a 3D convolutional neural network on track-weighted fractional anisotropy. This approach captures gene and brain associations from a multi-ethnic cohort of 4741 youth in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (age range: 9-10 years old). We fine-tune the model on separate held-out datasets for cross-sectional and 2-year follow-up prediction, respectively. Here we show that the model improves cross-sectional (266 participants) and two-year predictions of depression and suicidality, with area under the curve values of 0.61 to 0.66. It outperforms unimodal models, increasing accuracy over genetics-only and brain-only models. Explainable artificial intelligence identifies key white matter tracts, including the superior longitudinal fasciculus, cingulum, and corpus callosum, as primary predictive features. The model effectively generalizes to an independent Korean youth sample (age range: 9-17 years old), achieving an area under the curve of 0.67. This establishes the cross-ethnic scalability of integrating genetics with brain imaging. These findings highlight the promise of multimodal deep learning for precision psychiatry and early clinical intervention.

title: AMYPAD-PNHS: A Pan-European, Multi-Site & Multimodal MRI Dataset of Older Adults Without Dementia.
abstract: The Amyloid Imaging to Prevent Alzheimer's Disease Prognostic and Natural History Study (AMYPAD-PNHS) multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) dataset provides open-access longitudinal MRI data of 2759 cognitively normal or mild cognitive impairment individuals, encompassing (micro-)structural, physiological, and functional MRI sequences from 10 European parent cohorts. Processed and raw images, and image-derived (endo-)phenotypes, are organized in Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) standards and accessible upon request, to enhance generalizability and comparability between future neuroimaging studies. This dataset supports preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD) and aging-related research by enabling robust multimodal analyses of neurodegeneration, microvascular pathology, and structural and functional connectivity changes, facilitating advanced investigations into preclinical AD mechanisms, informing early intervention strategies and allowing reproducible and centralized neuroimaging (endo-)phenotyping.

title: Bulk RNA sequencing dataset of embryonic dorsal telencephalon and cerebral cortex from Sbno1 and Trp53 double conditional knockout mice.
abstract: Sbno1 (Strawberry notch homolog 1) encodes a nuclear protein expressed in neuronal populations and has been implicated in neurodevelopmental processes. However, bulk transcriptomic datasets from embryonic neural stem cells lacking Sbno1 are limited due to early embryonic lethality in conventional knockout models. To enable stage-specific transcriptomic characterization of Sbno1-deficient neural progenitors, we generated a dorsal telencephalon-specific Sbno1 and Trp53 double conditional knockout (dcKO) mouse model using the Emx1-Cre driver. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on dorsal telencephalon at embryonic day 12.5 (E12.5) and cerebral cortex at E18.5 from dcKO and littermate control mice. The dataset includes seven biological replicates across two developmental stages and was generated using paired-end 150 bp sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq X Plus platform. We provide raw sequencing reads, gene-level count matrices, normalized expression values, and associated metadata. Quality control metrics, alignment statistics, sample-level principal component analysis, and replicate concordance analyses are reported to document data quality and reproducibility. This dataset provides a resource for investigating transcriptional dynamics downstream of Sbno1 and Trp53 in embryonic cortical development, and for applying diverse computational and integrative analytical approaches.

title: Peroxiredoxin 3 deficiency promotes age-dependent dopaminergic neurodegeneration with mitochondrial redox abnormalities and oxidized dopamine-associated fluorescence.
Sex differences in polygenic risk for sex-biased brain disorders: Associations with diagnostic status and brain age gap.
abstract: Biological sex influences the prevalence and progression of several brain disorders, yet it remains unclear whether genetic risk interacts with sex in relation to case-control status or brain health. Using data from up to 220 836 females and 187 651 males in the UK Biobank (aged 39-81), we assessed how sex and polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for major depressive disorder (PRSMDD), Alzheimer's disease (PRSAD), schizophrenia (PRSSCZ), and Parkinson's disease (PRSPD) relate to case-control status and MRI-derived brain age gap (BAG) as a proxy of brain health. We tested for sex differences in PRSs and performed regression analyses examining associations between sex, PRSs, and both outcomes. We then compared models with sex-pooled or sex-specific PRSs to explore whether sex-specific PRSs improve predictive accuracy. PRSSCZ was higher in females, while no other PRSs differed by sex. A significant PRSAD-by-sex interaction revealed weaker associations with AD case-control status in males than females. Sex-pooled models outperformed sex-specific models for case-control status, apart from PRSAD, where the female-only PRSAD model outperformed the sex-pooled model. No sex-by-PRS interactions were significantly associated with BAG. However, male sex, higher PRSMDD, higher PRSAD, and lower PRSPD were associated with higher BAG, indicative of an older brain age. BAG model performance did not differ between sex-pooled and sex-specific PRS models. In summary, while sex-specific PRSs currently offer limited value over sex-pooled scores, the superior performance of the female-specific PRSAD model suggests that the value of sex-specific PRSs will likely grow with increased statistical power. Link to preregistration and preprint: https://osf.io/a8pt2/ .

title: A reproducible structural brain axis of alcohol use severity.
abstract: Alcohol use is linked to distributed structural brain alterations, but population-level alcohol-related neurobiology remains difficult to quantify. We tested whether deep learning-derived MRI representations capture reproducible variation in alcohol consumption severity and converge with clinical and biological markers. Representations were extracted from gray-matter volume maps in the German National Cohort (NAKO; N ≈ 28,000). Ridge-regression scores were derived from structural MRI to estimate alcohol consumption severity, measured with the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test-Consumption (AUDIT-C). Models were trained in NAKO, externally validated in UK Biobank (N ≈ 25,000), evaluated in FOR2107 (N ≈ 1900), and tested against ICD-10 alcohol use disorder (AUD), alcohol-related biomarkers, and cognition. In NAKO, the structural MRI-derived ridge-regression score correlated with measured AUDIT-C severity (r = 0.11; 95% CI, 0.09-0.12; qFDR = 1.2 × 10-70; MAE = 1.64). This association replicated in UK Biobank (r = 0.09; 95% CI, 0.07-0.10; qFDR = 4.9 × 10-41; MAE = 1.96) and generalized to AUD, with higher odds in the highest versus lowest brain-score quintile (OR = 2.28; 95% CI, 1.49-3.48; qFDR = 3.9 × 10-4). The score was associated with gamma-glutamyl transferase (β = 1.17 U/L; qFDR = 0.007), mean corpuscular volume (β = 14.26 fL; qFDR = 4.4 × 10-4), and slower reaction time (β = 163.40 ms; qFDR = 3.0 × 10-5). Deep learning-derived structural MRI representations capture weak but reproducible alcohol-related brain variation that converges with AUD diagnosis, peripheral biomarkers, and cognition, supporting their use in population-level addiction neuroscience while underscoring limits for individual-level prediction.

title: Pulvinar-cortical connectomic deviations identify symptom-relevant biotypes in schizophrenia.
abstract: Schizophrenia exhibits profound clinical heterogeneity, yet biologically interpretable imaging markers capturing symptom-specific variance remain elusive. Although the pulvinar is a critical higher-order thalamic hub for cortico-cortical coordination, whether its individualized abnormalities can define clinically meaningful biotypes remains unexplored. The present study implemented a symptom-guided normative modeling framework using multisite resting-state functional MRI data from 746 healthy controls and 387 patients with schizophrenia. Individualized pulvinar-cortical deviation profiles were estimated relative to a healthy reference model and integrated with symptom-guided feature selection and unsupervised clustering. Two partially separable biotypes were identified within a clinically enriched low-dimensional feature space. The biotypes were clinically anchored primarily in negative symptom severity, with a significant between-biotype difference that remained after adjustment for site and other available covariates. Symptom-relevant connections showed a structured cortical distribution concentrated predominantly in somatomotor, visual, and ventral attention networks. Imaging-transcriptomic analyses provided exploratory spatial molecular context, with Biotype 1 showing enrichment profiles involving translation, protein targeting, and synaptic organization, and Biotype 2 showing profiles involving neurodevelopment, synaptic remodeling, and metal-ion homeostasis. Site-exclusion analyses indicated partial stability of the biotype solution, although clinical separation varied across sites. Projection into an independent repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation cohort showed nominal, uncorrected differences in 2-week negative symptom improvement that were not sustained at 4 weeks and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating. These findings support a symptom-guided pulvinar-cortical framework for characterizing schizophrenia heterogeneity, while independent replication using prespecified models is required to establish clinical and biological validity.

title: Gene-environment interplay in internalising and externalising psychopathology in adolescence.
abstract: A combination of genetic and environmental factors working in interplay is thought to underlie differences in symptoms of psychopathology between adolescents. Yet, studies that have investigated gene-environment interaction in isolated aspects of developmental psychopathology lack robust effects, highlighting the need for a broader approach. We adopted a multivariable framework to investigate gene-environment interaction in internalising and externalising symptoms of psychopathology in a sample of 3337 16-year-olds from the Twins Early Development Study. We used penalised regression models to examine the main effects of genetic factors (G), indexed by combining 13 polygenic scores for psychopathology, and environmental factors (E), measured by combining multiple environmental exposures during childhood and adolescence, on symptoms of psychopathology. We also examined their additive effects (G+E) and their interaction (G×E). Polygenic scores accounted for, on average, 2.7% of the variance in symptoms of psychopathology, with stronger predictions for externalising symptoms, while environmental measures alone accounted for an average of 7.1% of the variance. G+E accounted for an average of 9.1% of differences between adolescents in symptoms of psychopathology. We observed small G×E effects for internalising symptoms, accounting for an average of 1.1% of the variance. Children with a higher genetic risk showed higher levels of internalising symptoms, especially when exposed to more chaos at home and harsher parenting. Our findings indicate that genetic and environmental influences contribute additively, underscoring the importance of jointly considering both factors to enhance our understanding of youth psychopathology. At the same time, our results highlight the persistent challenges involved in identifying robust G×E effects.

title: Distinct patterns of neural activity during initial defeat encounter are predictive of future susceptibility or resilience to chronic defeat.
abstract: Social stress is a significant factor in triggering psychiatric disorders, including depression. The effects of chronic stress accumulate, and the way in which an individual responds to those initial stress exposures can shape subsequent stress reactivity. The chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) model in mice has been used to examine neurobiological mechanisms underlying individual variability in stress outcomes. After 10 days of social defeat, mice diverge into distinct groups based on their social behavior: "resilient" mice maintain high social exploration whereas "susceptible" mice avoid social stimuli. Here, we used Fos-TRAP2 technology to permanently label neural activity on day 1 of defeat while allowing mice to undergo the full CSDS protocol and subsequent social interaction testing. Using a customized, high-throughput method for counting FosTRAP-positive cells across a total of 66 brain regions, we showed that social defeat provoked a brain-wide synchronization of neural activity. Moreover, the specific response patterns captured during that first defeat were dramatically different depending on whether mice would go on to develop a resilient vs. susceptible phenotype, suggesting that largely distinct networks of brain regions recruited during the initial experience shape the eventual behavioral outcome. Finally, within defeated mice, higher activation within paraventricular zone of the hypothalamus on day 1 correlated with more resilient social interaction ratios that emerged after several days of stress. This work represents a comprehensive description of the brain-wide neural network encoding social defeat, revealing how distinct neural responses to the initial defeat encounter precede the emergence of different coping behaviors after chronic defeat.

title: Brain-derived multi-omics prioritization of mitochondria-related genes in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in psychiatric disorders, yet the regulatory mechanisms linking brain-expressed mitochondrial genes to disease risk remain unclear. To investigate these mechanisms, we employed an integrative multi-omics approach combining brain-derived DNA methylation, gene expression, and protein abundance quantitative trait locus (QTL) datasets to evaluate genetically predicted associations of mitochondria related molecular traits with schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BD), major depressive disorder (MDD), cross-disorder phenotypes, and clinical subtypes. Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), Heterogeneity in dependent instruments (HEIDI) testing, and Bayesian colocalization analyses were applied, followed by a study-specific three-tier framework to prioritize potential putative causal genes. Our analyses prioritized ACADVL and SLC25A24 as Tier 1 genes for SCZ, COX11 as a Tier 2 gene for SCZ, and DLST, ENDOG, and PDF as Tier 3 genes for SCZ. ENDOG and PDF were also prioritized for the BD-SCZ cross-disorder phenotype. Further SMR analyses across molecular layers supported ENDOG as a methylation-linked regulatory signal, whereas expression-to-protein associations for COX11 and SLC25A24 showed colocalization support but did not meet the HEIDI criterion. Single-cell analyses suggested context-dependent ENDOG effects across immune cell types. Together, these findings support the involvement of mitochondria-related genes across molecular layers in psychiatric disorders and identify genetically supported candidate genes that warrant experimental validation.

title: Characterizing the Phenotype and Connectome of Relaxin Family Peptide Receptor 3 Expressing Cells in the Bed Nucleus of the Stria Terminalis in Female Mice.
abstract: RXFP3-expressing cells in the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNSTRXFP3 cells) are implicated in complex motivated behavior and are susceptible to adaptation following chronic stress. In the current study, we therefore sought to further understand the neurochemical phenotype and connectivity of BNSTRXFP3 neurons. First, we investigated the afferent connectome of BNSTRXFP3 cells via monosynaptic pseudorabies tracing. This identified strong inputs from the amygdala and hypothalamus. Regarding output targets of BNSTRXFP3 cells, viral anterograde tracing showed dense innervation of social, reproductive and motivational centers of the brain. BNSTRXFP3 innervation of the preoptic area of the hypothalamus (POA) was particularly pronounced. Given the sexually dimorphic role of the POA in social behavior, we focused on phenotyping the BNST → POA projection specifically in female mice. Our findings demonstrate that ∼83% of all labeled BNST → POA projection neurons coexpress Rfxp3 and ERα. Moreover, the overwhelming majority of Rxfp3-expressing BNST → POA projection neurons colocalized with Tac1 (∼80%), ERα (∼82%) or Cyp19a1 (Aromatase; ∼86%) in female mice. A subset of these cells express Slc17a6 that encodes VGluT2. These findings place BNSTRXFP3 cells within circuits implicated in stress, reward and complex social behaviors.

title: Neural Systems in the Siphonophore Nanomia septata: Overview of the Entire Colony.
abstract: Siphonophores are colonial hydrozoans with unprecedented differentiation and specialization, in which individual zooids are transformed into "functional organs" rather than autonomous polyps capable of feeding. As a result, the entire colony acts as a single, modular individual with the highest level of coordination and integration, from development through behavior. Deciphering these integrative mechanisms requires understanding the microanatomical organization of the nervous system across all elements of the colony. Here, using two immunohistochemical markers (anti-tubulin and anti-RFamide antibodies), we systematically characterize the neural systems across the entire Nanomia colony, encompassing the pneumatophore, stem, and all zooid classes (nectophores, gastrozooids, palpons, male and female gonophores, and protective zooids). Using two markers enables visualization of distinct neural subpopulations, some of which a single marker does not reveal. We provide evidence of neuroanatomical interactions within all elements of the colony, including contributions from giant axons, stem polygonal nets, and RFamide-ir neural rings at the base of each zooid, and describe distinct neural network subpopulations in various zooids. This mapping facilitates functional identification of novel conductive and signaling pathways for future analysis of the cellular basis of behavioral integration within decentralized, broadly distributed nets and the non-neuronal elements of these unique superorganisms.

title: Cortical Hypoperfusion in Acute Anorexia Nervosa Is Graded Along the Sensorimotor-Association Hierarchy.
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: Cortical gray-matter changes in anorexia nervosa (AN) are among the largest reported in psychiatry, but the functional-metabolic state of that tissue is largely unknown. Because cortical energy use is highest in transmodal association cortex (prefrontal, parietal, and temporal regions of the default-mode and frontoparietal networks), a reduced energy supply predicts a graded rather than uniform reduction in perfusion (blood delivery to tissue). A total of 44 acutely underweight women with AN and 45 healthy women underwent 3 T pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling with partial-volume correction. Cerebral blood flow was compared between groups across the Schaefer 100 regions 7 networks atlas, age-adjusted and false-discovery-rate-corrected, and the case-control map was compared with the principal functional gradient (the axis running from sensorimotor to transmodal cortex), with cortical thickness in the same participants, and with 18 PET and SPECT receptor maps. Perfusion was lower in AN in 97 of 100 regions and maximal in orbitofrontal and prefrontal cortex (composite d = -0.56). The deficit scaled with position along the principal functional gradient (ρ = -0.56), an axis unrelated to perfusion in health, and was recoverable in individual brains (d = -0.53). Thinning was widespread but unrelated to gradient position, and the two effect maps did not correspond. Hypoperfusion was greater where D1, CB1, mGluR5, M1, 5-HT2A, and μ-opioid systems are dense, the dopaminergic, cannabinoid, glutamatergic, and muscarinic ones persisting after gradient adjustment. Cortical perfusion in acute AN is not uniformly reduced but organized along the cortex's principal functional axis, dissociable from cortical thinning and aligned with reward-related neurochemistry.

title: Psychobiotics and the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis: Mechanistic Insights, Multi-Omics Advances, and Therapeutic Potential in Mental and Systemic Disorders.
abstract: Common mental illnesses, such as anxiety, depression, and neurodegenerative diseases, are increasing worldwide, and there is increasing evidence that their pathogenesis is associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis and disruption of the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA). Nevertheless, there is a lack of mechanistic understanding and clinical translation of psychobiotics. This review consolidates the results of preclinical, clinical, and multi-omics research to assess the role of psychobiotics, such as prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, and postbiotics, in regulating MGBA pathways, including endocrine, immune, neural, and metabolic pathways, along with developments in metabolite detection and microbial profiling. Psychobiotics normalize the intestinal microbial composition, increase the intestinal barrier integrity, and balance neuroinflammation. They modulate the levels of major neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin, γ-aminobutyric acid) and suppress hyperactivity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. There is growing evidence showing their therapeutic efficacy in gastrointestinal, metabolic, autoimmune, and neuropsychiatric diseases, including anxiety, depression, and Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Synergistic effects with neuro-nutrition and physical activity further enhance cognitive function and neuroplasticity. Psychobiotics provide a mechanism-based approach to address interconnected pathways of the MGBA, which is an exciting addition to traditional treatments with an excellent safety profile. Precision psychobiotic intervention and translation of multi-omics approaches into clinical practice require standardized and large-scale clinical trials as well as integration of these methods.

title: Mapping the two faces of the blood-brain barrier.
abstract: In brain capillaries, flattened endothelial cells separate the blood from the brain across luminal and abluminal membranes that are approximately 200 nm apart. Amick and colleagues now resolve this hidden polarity in vivo, identify sequence motifs that direct proteins towards the brain-facing membrane, and show that membrane distribution can change with the time of day.

title: Predictors Over Time of Occlusion Following Flow Diverter Treatment for Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysms: Insights from the INSPIRE-A Registry.
abstract: Flow diverters (FD) are integral to endovascular treatment-strategies for intracranial aneurysms. However, high-quality evidence on variables associated with procedural success after FD treatment is sparse and partially contradictory. To analyze factors associated with complete occlusion (Raymond Roy Occlusion Classification [RROC] I) of internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms at various follow-up (FU) time points. The INSPIRE-A registry is a prospective, single-arm study of aneurysms treated with FD. FU imaging was adjudicated by an independent imaging core laboratory. Patient characteristics, aneurysm details, and procedural variables were tested for association with RROC I at different FU (post-procedure, 6-,12-,24-month), using logistic regression analyses complemented by generalized estimating equations (GEE) across FU. Overall, 692 patients were included (median age, 55 years [IQR, 46-64]; 84.7% female). In multivariable analysis, adjunctive coiling was associated with RROC I post-procedure (aOR, 20.98; 95% CI, 6.27-70.22), older age at 6 and 12 months (aOR per year, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.99 and 0.95-1.00), male sex at 12 months (aOR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.17-0.58), and current smoking at 12 months (aOR, 2.53; 95% CI, 1.30-4.96). GEE showed that the effect of adjunctive coiling decreased over time, whereas neck width was associated with lower odds of RROC I at 12 and 24 months only. This dataset, with independent imaging core lab adjudication, suggests that adjunctive coiling promoted early occlusion, whereas age, sex, smoking status, and neck width influence complete occlusion at later FU after FD treatment of ICA aneurysms.

title: Multiple simultaneous acute infarcts in CADASIL: a retrospective cohort study and systematic review.
Associations between WHO-defined hyperglycemia in pregnancy and adverse outcomes in Malawi: a blinded prospective cohort study.
[Physical health in psychiatry: nurses at the heart of screening and prevention].
abstract: People living with a severe psychiatric disorder have a shorter life expectancy and higher mortality rates than the general population, primarily due to somatic conditions. In light of these challenges, nurses play a major role in identifying risk factors, providing clinical monitoring, coordinating the care pathway, and promoting health. Recent changes in nursing competencies - particularly regarding the ordering of certain diagnostic tests - could help strengthen efforts to prevent somatic conditions among this particularly vulnerable population.

title: [Mental health and physical health: a vital partnership].
abstract: Even today, people living with severe mental illness die 10 to 20 years earlier than the rest of the population, primarily from physical illnesses that are, in part, preventable. Because mental health cannot be separated from physical health, an integrated approach to care has become essential. Nurses play a central role in this transformation due to their role in identification, education, and coordination.

title: A Teenage Boy With Abdominal Contusion.
Effects of clinostat-based microgravity simulation on the growth and differentiation of cerebral organoids using a 3D-clinostat.
abstract: The human brain is highly sensitive to altered gravitational environments, yet the molecular and cellular consequences of microgravity remain poorly understood due to the limited accessibility of astronaut neural tissue. Here, we employ human cerebral organoids cultured in a 3D clinostat to clinostat-based simulation and investigate neurodevelopmental responses. Organoids were exposed to continuous clinostat-based simulation for 30 days (C30), 15 days followed by 15 days of normal gravity (C15 N15), or standard gravity controls (N30). Neurochemical profiling revealed marked reductions in acetylcholine, dopamine, norepinephrine, and glutamate under microgravity, with partial recovery after re-adaptation; by contrast, GABA levels increased persistently, suggesting an excitatory-inhibitory imbalance. Transcriptomic analysis demonstrated widespread downregulation of pluripotency markers (OCT4, NANOG, SOX2), regional identity genes (FOXG1, DLX2, NKX2.1, SIX6), and neuronal differentiation markers (MAP2, DCX, VGLUT1), whereas astrocytic GFAP was robustly elevated and cortical identity marker SATB2 recovered upon re-exposure to normal gravity. Despite extensive transcriptional changes, protein levels of the neuronal marker MAP2 and the pluripotency marker SOX2 remained unchanged. Together, these findings indicate that clinostat-based simulation disrupts stemness, regional specification, and neurotransmitter balance, while promoting astrocytic lineage bias and partial recovery upon gravitational re-exposure. This study establishes human cerebral organoids as a tractable ground-based simulation model for probing brain vulnerability to space environments and for identifying candidate biomarkers and countermeasures to safeguard astronaut neurocognitive health during long-duration missions.

title: Exposure to low (10 cGy) doses of simulated space radiation impairs reward-guided decision making in both male and female rats.
abstract: Decision-making under uncertainty depends on coordinated frontostriatal circuitry that integrates reward valuation, outcome monitoring, and cognitive control. Perturbations within this network can bias strategy selection, favoring immediate or uncertain rewards, without overtly impairing learning or motivation. Such subtle changes in decision bias may have significant operational consequences for astronauts, whose performance during long-duration missions will depend on maintaining cognitive flexibility and risk evaluation. During deep space travel, astronauts will be exposed to Space Radiation (SR), a complex field of highly energetic charged particles. Estimated cumulative doses during Mars-class missions may reach 1-1.2 Sv (∼200 cGy), raising concerns about its effects on brain function. Preclinical studies demonstrate that such SR doses disrupts dopamine-dependent cognition, alters striatal dopamine turnover and receptor expression, and perturbs oscillatory signaling that coordinates frontostriatal activity. Low-dose SR exposure in rodents produces decision-making alterations across multiple frontostriatal-dependent tasks, including the Associative Recognition Memory Interference Touchscreen (ARMIT) and the rat Risk Taking Predisposition task (rRTP), manifesting as changes in flexibility and decision bias rather than overt deficits. Moreover, SR effects are sex dependent: males exhibit slower response times (increased switch cost), whereas females maintain speed at the expense of accuracy, suggesting distinct compensatory mechanisms. Here, we show that exposure to 10 cGy of the Simplified Galactic Cosmic Radiation Simulator (SGS) alters cost-benefit decision-making in the rRTP in both sexes. SGS-exposed males displayed a global degradation of reward sensitivity, consistent with striatal dopaminergic dysfunction, whereas females exhibited a selective shift toward high-risk, low-probability choices, implicating orbitofrontal disruption of fine-grained value discrimination. These outcomes reflect distinct but converging failures of dopaminergic precision and cortical-striatal coordination. We propose a threshold-based model of cognitive reserve in which males rely primarily on striatal integrity and females on orbitofrontal precision. Once these sex-specific compensatory networks are exceeded, executive control deteriorates along divergent trajectories, revealing complementary mechanisms of radiation-induced cognitive vulnerability.

title: Caffeine consumption aboard the International Space Station and its relationship to sleep and cognitive performance.
abstract: Caffeine is a widely consumed performance-enhancing stimulant on Earth that also affects sleep outcomes. Though historically available on spaceflight missions, caffeine use and its influence on sleep and human performance in microgravity have yet to be evaluated. We combined archival data on caffeine use, sleep, and cognitive performance aboard the International Space Station to determine astronauts' consumption patterns and to characterize the relationships between caffeine consumption, sleep, and cognitive performance during spaceflight. All crewmembers with available data consumed caffeine (mean of 105 mg per day), a value lower than daily use in the regular population, and there were small but significant effects of caffeine on that night's sleep as well as of sleep on caffeine consumed the following day. Caffeine consumption also led to faster reaction times on cognitively demanding tasks. Though the data are limited, they provide important information about crew consumption habits which will be of use in future mission planning.

title: Decoupling musculoskeletal integrity in microgravity: Molecular drivers and therapeutic horizons.
abstract: The numerous physiological, environmental, and psychological challenges of spaceflight and extended space missions greatly impact an astronaut's health. Microgravity exposure during spaceflight leads to a profound decline of musculoskeletal integrity, characterized by a marked reduction in muscle mass and bone microarchitecture, and impaired muscle-bone crosstalk. These changes pose serious risks to astronauts' long-term health and provide a valuable model for studying disuse-related musculoskeletal disorders on Earth. This paper highlights the current understanding of ground-based preclinical and clinical experimental models that effectively simulate microgravity-related unloading and complement data from real spaceflight missions. Microgravity affects key molecular drivers by disrupting signalling pathways (PI3K/AKT/mTOR, ubiquitin-proteasome, Wnt/β-catenin, and RANKL), thereby disrupting the balance between protein synthesis and proteolysis, altering calcium homeostasis, and increasing bone resorption. Additionally, dysregulated myokines and osteokines play a pivotal role in uncoupling bone-muscle communication, intensifying tissue degeneration. This narrative review aims to consolidate recent evidence from PubMed and Google Scholar on the effects of real and simulated microgravity (SMG) on the musculoskeletal system, critically assessing molecular pathways and the integrating roles of myokines and osteokines in muscle-bone crosstalk associated with microgravity. Additionally, it critically evaluates the effectiveness of major countermeasures used in both spaceflight and experimental models. It outlines future directions for developing integrative, personalized countermeasures that combine mechanical, metabolic, and molecular approaches to preserve musculoskeletal health in long-term space missions and similar clinical conditions on Earth.

title: Traditional Vedic Sanskrit education and intrinsic brain organization: a cross-sectional resting-state fMRI study.
abstract: Vedic Sanskrit recitation is an intensive oral tradition involving memorization, repeated retrieval, phonological precision, rhythmic production, and sustained attention, and we examined whether long-term training is associated with specific memory performance and intrinsic brain organization. Thirty Vedic scholars and 30 non-Vedic men aged 21-28 years completed the PGI Memory Scale and resting-state functional MRI. Groups were compared on memory subtests, amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF), local correlation (LCOR), functional-connectivity multivoxel pattern analysis (fc-MVPA) and ROI-to-ROI connectivity, adjusting for age and Raven score with false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction. Within scholars, training history was related to these measures. Scholars showed a large, selective advantage in immediate recall (adjusted difference = 2.51 points, 95% CI [1.68, 3.34]; adjusted d = 1.92; FDR-adjusted p = 9.4 × 10-7); no other subtest differed after correction. Scholars had greater ALFF in a cerebellar-posterior cluster (pFDR = .003), greater LCOR in cerebellar and postcentral-parietal clusters but lower LCOR in occipital and right anterior temporal clusters. fc-MVPA identified 10 clusters with distinct connectivity patterns, and ROI-to-ROI analysis a network with predominantly lower coupling in scholars (pFDR = .048). Within scholars, training variables were associated with ALFF, LCOR and fc-MVPA in thalamic, medial temporal, frontal and sensorimotor regions. No brain-behaviour or training-memory correlation survived correction. Long-term Vedic oral education was associated with better immediate recall and distinct intrinsic organization of language- and memory-related brain systems, supporting further longitudinal study.

title: Literacy training in kindergarten children using pencil, virtual keyboard, or tablet stylus: Writing-medium effects on training-induced event-related potential modulations during letter viewing.
abstract: The effects of handwriting training on letter recognition, compared with typing, have mainly been discussed in terms of either action-perception coupling or visual learning processes. To clarify the underlying mechanisms, this study examined how different writing media during literacy acquisition affect event-related potential (ERP) modulations during a sequential letter-matching task in kindergarten children. The analyzed sample comprised 77 children (4.9-6.9 years), who completed 28 sessions of standardized training involving 16 letters using handwriting with pencil and paper, handwriting with a stylus on a tablet, or typing on a virtual keyboard. Before and after training, children performed a sequential character-matching task with letters and pseudoletters while EEG was recorded. Training-related ERP effects to letters were observed in occipital P1, N1, and N2 components and centro-parietal ERPs within the P2 time window, but not in ERPs at central electrodes associated with motor representations. ERP changes emerged following both handwriting with pencil and paper and typing training but not following stylus-based handwriting. Only the pencil group showed training-related left-lateralized increases of N1 amplitude to real letters. The ERP effects of the intervention primarily reflect visual learning processes rather than the reactivation of graphomotor memory traces. The left-lateralized N1 increase following handwriting with pencil and paper indicates that the writing medium influences the visual processing of learned letters. The absence of effects following handwriting with stylus may reflect the higher motor-control demands of writing on a slippery tablet surface or the poorer quality of the visual letter output.

title: Corrigendum to "self-directed dramatic and music play programs enhance executive function in Japanese children", [Trends in Neuroscience and Education, (2021) 24, 100158].
The double burden: parent PTSD and economic hardship as predictors of child PTSD during continuous trauma.
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Parent posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and family-level economic hardship may both contribute to child PTSD risk during continuous trauma exposure. While different theoretical approaches vary in the direction of effects they propose, this study aims to advance a family-level framework in which economic hardship and parental PTSD operate as mutually reinforcing processes that jointly shape child PTSD risk under continuous trauma. Data were drawn from a longitudinal study conducted during the regional conflict following the October 7th attack among parents of children (N = 1,659), which comprised two subsamples: a representative sample of the Israeli adult population (n = 973) and an oversample of high-risk populations with heightened war-related exposure and socioeconomic impact (n = 686). Parents reported their own PTSD symptoms, children's PTSD symptoms, war exposure, and objective indicators of economic hardship. Analyses included regression models and longitudinal path analyses to examine directionality between parent PTSD symptoms and economic hardship and their contributions to subsequent child PTSD symptoms. Parent PTSD symptoms and economic hardship were robustly associated with child PTSD symptoms, even after accounting for levels of war exposure. Families experiencing a double burden of elevated parent PTSD symptoms and economic hardship had the highest levels of child PTSD symptoms. In longitudinal analyses, parent PTSD symptoms consistently predicted child PTSD symptoms across subsamples, while economic hardship predicted child PTSD symptoms among high-risk families but not in the representative subsample. Findings highlight the importance of understanding child PTSD within a broader family context during continuous trauma. Parent PTSD and economic hardship may function as interconnected risk processes, with particularly strong implications for children in highly affected populations. Interventions targeting both parent mental health and family-level economic stressors may be critical for reducing child PTSD risk under conditions of ongoing trauma.

title: Suspended TiO2/AlGaN/GaN Synaptic-Like Photodetectors With Integrated Microheaters for Spatially Resolved UV Discharge Monitoring.
abstract: Partial discharge in power grids emits weak ultraviolet (UV) signals, yet continuous spatial imaging with sensitivity remains challenging for conventional sensors. Although standard photodetectors suffer from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and high-power consumption, synaptic-like designs utilizing persistent photoconductance (PPC) address these issues through in-sensor integration but face difficulty in resetting the conductance state. We demonstrate a suspended TiO2/AlGaN/GaN synaptic-like UV photodetector with an on-chip Pt microheater. Oxygen vacancies in TiO2 and donor‑impurity X (DX) centers in AlGaN serve as optically writable and thermally erasable traps that modulate the AlGaN/GaN two‑dimensional electron gas (2DEG), enabling time‑integrated sensing and thermal reset. The suspended membrane confines Joule heating to the active region, allowing reset within 2 s. Under 365 nm at 0.42 µW/cm2, the device exhibits a photoconductive gain of 2.8 × 107 and a responsivity of 2.12 × 106 A/W, with stable operation over 120 cycles. A 3 × 3 array enables spatially resolved detection with improved contrast, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) distinguishes corona‑ and arc‑like patterns from simulated images. These results support the use of this detector array for partial discharge inspection in power systems.

title: Biomarker-informed differences in treatment-associated cognitive decline in dementia with Lewy bodies.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) co-pathology is common in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) and has been linked to worse clinical outcomes. Whether AD biomarker status influences cognitive trajectories and treatment-associated cognitive trajectories in DLB remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective cohort study by linking the Swedish Registry for Cognitive/Dementia Disorders (SveDem) with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker data. Participants were individuals with incident DLB diagnosed between 2010 and 2020 who had CSF amyloid-β42/amyloid-β40 (Aβ42/40) or Aβ42/phosphorylated tau (p-tau) measurements and longitudinal Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) assessments during follow-up. Linear mixed-effects models incorporating inverse probability of treatment and censoring weighting estimated cognitive trajectories according to AD biomarker status and antidementia treatment. Among 360 participants (mean age 73.3 years; 33.9% women), 196 (54.4%) were AD biomarker-positive. AD biomarker-positive participants exhibited faster cognitive decline than biomarker-negative participants, with an additional decline of 0.80 MMSE points per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.17 to -0.43). Overall, cholinesterase inhibitor (ChEI) use was associated with slower cognitive decline than no treatment, whereas associations for memantine were less consistent. In biomarker-stratified analyses, ChEI use was associated with slower decline among AD biomarker-positive participants but not among biomarker-negative participants. Formal interaction analyses indicated that treatment-associated differences in MMSE change varied according to AD biomarker status. AD biomarker positivity identifies a subgroup of individuals with DLB at higher risk of accelerated cognitive decline. Treatment-associated cognitive trajectories also differed according to AD biomarker status; however, these observational treatment findings require cautious interpretation and confirmation in prospective biomarker-stratified studies.

title: FAM50A restrains METTL3-METTL14 catalytic activity to regulate m6A deposition and cell proliferation.
abstract: N 6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most abundant internal modification in eukaryotic messenger RNA (mRNA) and is substantially deposited co-transcriptionally by the METTL3-METTL14 methyltransferase complex. However, how chromatin-associated factors modulate the catalytic activity of the m6A writer complex remains poorly understood. Here, we identify FAM50A as a chromatin-associated negative regulator of m6A deposition. Histone TurboID-based chromatin proteomics and biochemical analyses revealed that FAM50A directly interacts with METTL3. Acute depletion of FAM50A resulted in a global increase in mRNA m6A modification, as demonstrated by quantitative, single-nucleotide-resolution GLORI. Mechanistically, FAM50A directly restrains METTL3-METTL14 methyltransferase activity without interfering with RNA substrate binding, thereby limiting excessive m6A deposition. Increased m6A following FAM50A depletion exerted transcript-dependent effects on mRNA stability, promoting destabilization of a subset of proliferation-associated transcripts while stabilizing others. These changes disrupted proliferation-associated gene-expression programs and impaired cell proliferation and viability. Furthermore, pathogenic FAM50A variants associated with Armfield X-linked intellectual disability exhibited defective m6A regulation and impaired cellular functions. Together, our findings identify FAM50A as a chromatin-associated restraint on METTL3-METTL14 activity that maintains m6A homeostasis and links epitranscriptomic regulation to cell proliferation and human disease.

title: Plasma D- and L-2-hydroxyglutarate during vorasidenib treatment of isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant glioma: development and validation of an enantioselective LC-MS/MS assay.
abstract: Mutant forms of isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 and 2 (IDH1/2) produce D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2-HG), which may serve as a circulating marker of biochemical target engagement during treatment with vorasidenib, an oral, brain-penetrant inhibitor of mutant IDH1/2. We aimed to develop an enantioselective LC-MS/MS assay for plasma D-2-HG and L-2-HG and evaluate its ability to detect longitudinal pharmacodynamic changes during treatment. We developed an LC-MS/MS assay for plasma D-2-HG and L-2-HG using protein precipitation, diacetyl-L-tartaric anhydride derivatization, reversed-phase separation, isotope-labeled internal standards, and stripped-serum surrogate calibration. Analytical performance was evaluated over the 6.75-2,030 nmol/L measuring interval. The assay was applied to baseline, 3-month, and 6-month samples from 36 patients with IDH-mutant grade 2 glioma receiving vorasidenib. Both enantiomers were baseline-resolved within a 10-min run.
