The lower limit of quantification was 6.75 nmol/L. Relative error remained within ±15 % at all calibration levels, and short-term between-run CVs in plasma-based QC materials were 2.3-5.7 %. Median D-2-HG decreased from 265 nmol/L (IQR, 223-305) at baseline to 121 nmol/L (IQR, 95-160) at 3 months and 128 nmol/L (IQR, 82-174) at 6 months. Model-estimated concentrations were 53.3 % lower at 3 months and 53.8 % lower at 6 months than at baseline, with no difference between follow-up visits (p=0.88). L-2-HG showed no significant time effect (p=0.53). The assay provided sensitive, reproducible, enantiomer-specific quantification of plasma 2-HG and detected early, sustained D-2-HG suppression during vorasidenib treatment. It supports pharmacodynamic assessment of mutant IDH inhibition. External validation and studies relating metabolite changes to clinical outcomes are needed before broader clinical implementation.

title: Pancreatic Steatosis as a Silent Culprit in Chronic Inflammatory States Such as Neurodegeneration: A Call for New Terminology (Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Pancreatic Disease or Metabolic Dysfunction- Associated Fatty Pancreas).
journal: The Turkish journal of gastroenterology : the official journal of Turkish Society of Gastroenterology

title: When resilience breaks down: Erosion of the protective role of intelligence in PTSD under extreme combat stress.
abstract: Resilience factors play an important role in shaping posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) trajectories, yet their protective effects may depend on the severity of trauma exposure. Prior research has linked higher premorbid IQ to lower PTSD risk, with longitudinal evidence from deploying soldiers showing more favorable symptom trajectories among those with higher IQ during routine combat deployment. The present study examined whether this protective effect persisted under conditions of extreme and protracted combat exposure during the Israel-Hamas war. Male Israel Defense Force infantry reservists (N = 192; Mean age at enrollment = 19.60 years, SD = 0.78; range = 19-23) were assessed for IQ at age 17 and followed across four time points: three during mandatory service with routine deployments and one during active reserve duty in the war. Ethnicity data were not collected. A mixed-design ANCOVA revealed an interaction (η2p = 0.017) indicating that higher IQ was associated with greater resilience under routine combat deployment conditions. However, this advantage disappeared under the extreme and protracted combat conditions of the war. Findings highlight that the protective role of cognitive ability is context-dependent, supporting diathesis-stress and threshold models of PTSD risk and resilience. Developmental implications associated with war-related trauma exposure during the critical period of emerging adulthood are discussed.

title: Fluorinated Poly(malic acid), a Water-Soluble Biodegradable Polymer to Stabilize Microbubbles for Ultrasound-Induced Blood-Brain Barrier Opening and Prolonged Imaging.
abstract: Clinical lipid-based microbubbles suffer from limited in vivo persistence and rely on organic solvent-based formulations, restricting emerging ultrasound applications including blood-brain barrier opening and ultrasound localization microscopy. To address these limitations, we report the synthesis of a new class of water-soluble fluorinated biodegradable polymer based on poly(malic acid) grafted with different percentages of short fluorinated moieties. This material, distinct from previous fluorinated polymers, enables the direct formulation of perfluorocarbon-microbubbles in water, without any organic solvent nor the use of lipids. The fluorinated moieties confer exceptional interfacial properties to the polymer, enhancing gas-shell interactions, leading to improved stability compared to the commercial lipid agent SonoVue and ultrasound responsiveness. In vivo, decafluorobutane polymer-stabilized microbubbles exhibit prolonged circulation, achieving a fourfold increase in hepatic mean transit time in mice (326 vs. 75 s) and a twofold increase in cerebral half-life in rats assessed by ultrasound localization microscopy (83 vs. 46 s). Safe and effective BBB-opening was achieved at mechanical indices of 0.25 and above, without detectable brain damage. By combining solvent-free formulation, lipid-free composition, tunable fluorination, and improved in vivo persistence, fluorinated poly(malic acid) microbubbles represent a promising and robust alternative to SonoVue for contrast imaging and BBB-opening applications.

title: Longitudinal patterns of problematic internet use and subsequent mental health problems in adolescents.
abstract: To evaluate the association between longitudinal patterns of problematic internet use (PIU) and later adolescent mental health, addressing time-varying confounding not fully accounted for in prior research. Longitudinal data were obtained from 3,171 adolescents who participated in the Tokyo Teen Cohort (2012-2021). PIU at ages 12 and 14 was categorized into tertiles (low, medium and high) to define longitudinal patterns. We applied the g-formula to estimate associations between these PIU patterns and mental health outcomes at age 16, accounting for baseline and time-varying confounders. Adolescents with persistently high PIU at ages 12 and 14 had higher risk and severity of mental health problems at age 16 compared with those with persistently low PIU: internalizing symptoms (risk difference [RD] 4.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.8%-7.6%; risk ratio [RR] 2.19, 95% CI 1.35-3.68; mean difference 1.21, 95% CI 0.49-1.95), depression (RD 6.3%, 95% CI 1.8-10.8%; RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.18-2.48; mean difference 0.97, 95% CI 0.33-1.64), anxiety (RD 5.0%, 95% CI 2.0-8.2%; RR 2.06, 95% CI 1.33-3.36; mean difference 0.64, 95% CI 0.26-1.03) and externalizing symptoms (RD 7.0%, 95% CI 3.9-10.0%; RR 3.21, 95% CI 1.84-6.56; mean difference 1.19, 95% CI 0.72-1.68). Patterns in which PIU remitted showed weaker and less consistent associations. Associations with depression were more pronounced in girls. The present study showed that persistent PIU is associated with subsequent internalizing, depressive, anxiety and externalizing symptoms in adolescents. Remission of PIU may be associated with attenuated severity. Approaches to reduce PIU appear indicated, which may include home-, school- and population-level interventions.

title: Analytical validation of an in-house CSF neurogranin assay for clinical use.
abstract: Synaptic dysfunction is an early and central feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) neurogranin (Ng) has emerged as a promising biomarker reflecting synaptic pathology. However, despite its increasing use in research, comprehensive analytical and clinical validation supporting its routine clinical use remains limited. We developed an updated version of an in-house CSF Ng enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (UGOT-Ng) and performed a full analytical validation, including precision, selectivity, measurement range, dilution linearity, interference, and sample stability. Method comparison with a previous assay version and instrument comparability were also assessed. A distribution-derived upper threshold was established using a large set of prospectively measured routine clinical samples. Finally, the associations between CSF Ng concentrations and core AD biomarkers were examined in a large retrospective dataset. The assay demonstrated acceptable analytical performance, with good repeatability and intermediate precision across the evaluated concentration levels. The measurement range was established at 38-1,200 ng/L, with satisfactory dilution linearity and minimal interference from blood contamination. CSF Ng showed high stability under various preanalytical conditions. Distribution-derived analysis in amyloid-negative clinical samples yielded an upper limit of 390 ng/L. In clinical samples, CSF Ng correlated strongly with total tau and phosphorylated tau, while associations with Aβ42/40 were weaker and largely driven by differences between amyloid-positive and -negative individuals. This study provides a comprehensive analytical validation of an in-house CSF Ng assay, supporting its implementation in a routine clinical laboratory. CSF Ng was strongly associated with CSF total tau and phosphorylated tau, supporting its relationship with tau-associated neuronal and synaptic pathology in AD. However, the strength of these correlations also raises the possibility that CSF Ng provides information that overlaps with established tau biomarkers. Further studies should therefore determine whether Ng offers incremental diagnostic or prognostic value, identifies biologically distinct patient subgroups, or improves the monitoring of synaptic dysfunction beyond currently available biomarkers.

title: The prevalence of multiple sclerosis (MS) in the American continent: a systematic review.
abstract: America is a continent covering more than 42,549,000 km2 and making up most of the land in the western hemisphere of the Earth. Thirty-five countries are located in the American continent. The prevalence of multiple sclerosis (MS) in different countries of America varies, so we designed this systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the pooled prevalence of MS in the American continent. We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and also references of included studies, review articles, and conference abstracts on 1 December 2022. Fifty studies were included. Most studies were conducted in the United States of America (USA) (between 1915 and 2020) and Canada (between 1982 and 2014). Crude prevalence rates of MS per 100,000 population varied substantially across the Americas, ranging from as low as 0.5-5 in parts of Brazil, Colombia, Panama, and Argentina to more than 300 in several high-prevalence regions of Canada and recent national estimates from the United States. Across the continent, MS prevalence has shown a consistent upward trend over time. A marked female predominance was consistently observed, with female-to-male ratios generally ranging from 2.0 to 3.6 across studies. The result of this systematic review showed that the prevalence of MS differs dramatically in the America continent with marked geographical heterogeneity consistent with the established latitudinal gradient.

title: Catheter tip placement for intrathecal therapy in refractory cancer pain: a systematic review.
abstract: Intrathecal drug delivery (IDD) provides continuous administration of analgesics into the intrathecal space. Although catheter tip placement is considered important for treatment success, evidence of its impact on long-term clinical outcomes remains limited, particularly when considering pain distribution, cancer type, and the intrathecal medication used. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the evidence of catheter tip positioning in patients with refractory cancer pain. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and EMBASE were systematically searched from inception to October 2025. Studies including patients with refractory cancer pain treated with implanted IDD were included. Study quality was assessed using a modified Downs and Black checklist. Meta-regression was performed to evaluate associations between treatment success and catheter tip location, pain distribution, and intrathecal medication type. Of 8,414 identified articles, 23 studies were included (14 in meta-analysis). Catheter tip placement descriptively corresponded to cancer type and pain location. However, meta-regression analyses showed no significant association between treatment success and catheter tip location (p = 0.914), pain location (p = 0.407), or intrathecal medication category (p = 0.937). Descriptive findings support anatomically guided catheter placement, but the available evidence is insufficient to determine whether catheter tip location or other examined factors are associated with treatment success. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251150374 identifier is CRD420251150374.

title: A Pilot Investigation of Endocannabinoid System Markers and Lipopolysaccharide Responses to 10 Sessions of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy.
journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
abstract: BACKGROUND Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) can modulate inflammatory and redox-sensitive pathways, but its effects on endocannabinoid system markers remain unclear. This exploratory biomarker subanalysis of a randomized controlled parent trial evaluated whether repeated HBOT was associated with changes in serum anandamide (AEA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) as primary outcomes. Cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2R), fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), and the baseline AEA-LPS association were assessed secondarily or exploratorily. MATERIAL AND METHODS The resource-limited, post-randomization sample included 17 healthy, physically active men: 9 from a pre-existing morning scheduling subgroup of the frequent-treatment HBOT arm and 8 controls selected before biomarker assays to improve baseline body mass index (BMI) comparability. HBOT consisted of 10 sessions performed 6 times weekly. Each session involved 60 minutes of 100% oxygen at 2.5 atmospheres absolute, delivered as three 20-min oxygen-breathing periods separated by two 5-minute air breaks. Fasting serum was collected before and after the protocol, and biomarkers were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. RESULTS No significant between-group differences in change scores were found for AEA (p = 0.597), CB2R (p=1.000), FAAH (p=0.885), or LPS (p=0.885). No significant within-group changes occurred in the HBOT group. Baseline AEA was positively associated with baseline LPS (Spearman's rho=0.505, p=0.039). CONCLUSIONS Receiving 10 HBOT sessions were not associated with significant changes in the measured circulating biomarkers. These exploratory findings do not exclude smaller effects, and the baseline AEA-LPS association requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.

title: Associations of Diagnosed Herpesvirus Infections and Antiviral Use With Multiple Sclerosis, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Nationwide Danish Cohort Study.
abstract: Diagnosed herpesvirus infections have been associated with several neurological and autoimmune diseases. We examined associations of recorded herpesvirus diagnoses, antiviral use, and HIV status with subsequent risk of multiple sclerosis (MS), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We conducted a nationwide Danish registry-based cohort study (1995-2018) including 48,897 individuals with a recorded HSV-1/2, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), or varicella-zoster virus (VZV) diagnosis and 546,890 matched comparators. In a separate analysis, 5737 individuals with HIV were compared with 58,160 matched comparators. Diagnoses of MS, ALS, or SLE ≥ 5 years after infection were primary outcomes. We estimated 20-year cumulative incidence and fitted absolute risk regression models in a competing-risk framework. The 20-year cumulative incidence of the composite outcome (MS, ALS, or SLE) was 0.66% among individuals with a recorded herpesvirus diagnosis and 0.38% among comparators (p < 0.001). Disease-specific cumulative incidence was higher for MS (0.50% vs. 0.24%, p < 0.001), similar for ALS (0.08% vs. 0.07%, p = 0.37), and slightly higher for SLE in the unadjusted analysis (0.097% vs. 0.07%, p = 0.04). After adjustment for antiviral-use category, the model estimate for MS was 1.35 (95% CI 1.03-1.78, p = 0.03), whereas estimates for ALS and SLE were not significant. Composite-outcome incidence was higher for recorded HSV-1/2 and EBV diagnoses, but not CMV. In the HIV analysis, the composite outcome occurred in 3/5737 individuals with HIV and 119/58,160 comparators (p = 0.01). This nationwide study supports an epidemiological association between a recorded diagnosis and later MS risk, whereas no adjusted association was observed for ALS or SLE.

title: Self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb motor recovery in people with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: This review examined the efficacy of self-guided, home-based rehabilitation (SGHBR) for upper limb recovery in people with stroke (PwS). PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and PEDro were searched using terms related to stroke, upper limb, home-based rehabilitation, and self-rehabilitation. Included articles were randomized controlled trials involving adults with stroke receiving home-based upper limb rehabilitation assessed with standardized clinical scales. Studies were excluded if the SGHBR intervention involved technological devices, telerehabilitation, or direct therapist supervision. Four reviewers screened 501 records, and 14 articles were included in the systematic review. Eight independent cohorts from 10 studies provided data for meta-analysis; remaining findings were narratively synthesized. SGHBR showed no significant advantage over other rehabilitation interventions, although the pooled estimate slightly favored SGHBR (SMD = 0.10, 95% CI -0.23 to 0.44), with low-to-moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 31.8%). Methodological quality was overall moderate, with variable risk of bias. Interventions differed in structure, duration, and strategies, but most included task-oriented or task-specific practice. SGHBR may provide upper limb functional benefits comparable to conventional therapy, but higher-quality studies are needed to confirm efficacy, generalizability, and cost-effectiveness across stroke survivor populations in routine practice.

title: Reply to: "Removing a Risk-Factor Label Is Not an Intervention That Prevents Parkinson's Disease".
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society

title: Engineered autophagy receptors for selective protein clearance in neurodegeneration.
abstract: Engineered autophagy receptors offer a way to direct intracellular degradation toward proteins implicated in neurodegeneration. Guo and colleagues fused cytoplasm-stable antibody fragments to microtubule-associated protein 1A/1B-light chain 3 alpha (LC3A) and delivered the resulting constructs using small extracellular vesicles. Their experiments show reduced pathological tau and cytoplasmic TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) in neuronal cultures and reduced tau pathology in mice. A separate adeno-associated virus experiment reduces TDP-43 pathology and improves motor performance in mice. These findings connect selective cargo recognition with intracellular delivery and raise questions about how engineered autophagy receptors might be adapted to different disease contexts. Here, we discuss which pathological protein assemblies are most accessible to these receptors, how selective clearance interacts with neuronal autophagic capacity, and how intracellular exposure relates to sustained functional benefit. We consider these questions with particular attention to preserving physiological protein function and linking cargo turnover to neuronal outcomes.

title: rTMS Attenuates Microglial Phagocytosis and Promotes Neurorepair in a Photothrombotic Stroke Mouse Model.
abstract: This study investigated the effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on functional recovery in photothrombotic (PT) stroke mice and whether rTMS promotes neurorepair by modulating microglial phagocytosis. Eight-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were used to establish a focal stroke model via photothrombosis (PT group). The Sham group and PT + rTMS group were included. rTMS was initiated 24 h after modeling. Neurological deficits were assessed. Microglial activation, synaptic phagocytosis, neuronal injury, and the levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) were evaluated. Differentially expressed proteins and core regulatory pathways were analyzed. rTMS treatment significantly increased body weight, prolonged the latency to fall and shortened the balance beam crossing time, reduced foot faults, and improved the discrimination index in PT mice. rTMS reduced the number of Iba1-positive microglia and CD68-positive cells, attenuated microglial synaptic phagocytosis, and alleviated neuronal loss and apoptosis. rTMS significantly decreased the levels of TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β in the brain. A total of 416 differentially expressed proteins were identified between the PT and PT + rTMS groups. The differentially expressed proteins were significantly enriched in microglial phagocytosis pathways and related signaling pathways. rTMS significantly ameliorates neurological deficits and cognitive impairment in PT stroke mice. The underlying mechanism may involve the inhibition of excessive microglial activation, attenuation of microglia-mediated synaptic phagocytosis, and alleviation of neuroinflammation. Proteomic analysis reveals that rTMS modulates the expression of proteins associated with microglial phagocytosis-related signaling pathways, which may contribute to the observed post-stroke neurorepair effects.

title: Intracellular Particle Burden Determines Effect on Macrophage Phagocytic Function in Response to Micro- and Nanoplastics Exposure.
authors: van den Berg Annemijne E T
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as emerging contaminants, yet their effects on immune health remain poorly understood. As professional phagocytes, macrophages are among the first immune cells to interact with foreign materials and have been shown to internalize MNPs. In this study, we investigated how MNP exposure influences macrophage phagocytic capacity, with emphasis on the intracellular particle burden. Human macrophages were exposed to model polystyrene (PS) particles and environmentally relevant materials, including ultraviolet (UV)-weathered PS, fragmented polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and cryomilled rubber particles, across a concentration range of 1-100 µg/mL. Particle uptake was confirmed using brightfield images, obtained by image-enhanced flow cytometry, revealing substantial heterogeneity in MNP internalization across the cell population. At the population level, MNP exposure had limited effects on phagocytosis of bacteria and tumor cells, except for enhanced tumor cell uptake following repeated exposure to high concentrations of UV-weathered PS. However, stratification by intracellular particle burden showed significantly increased phagocytic activity in highly loaded cells, compared to cells with low or no uptake. Overall, this study demonstrates an increase in phagocytic capacity dependent on internal particle concentration, indicating that alterations in macrophage function may be overlooked when internal particle burden is not considered.

title: Thiol reactivity and ferroptosis sensitization as toxic mechanisms of the phthalimide pesticides folpet and captan.
journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology
abstract: Captan and folpet are phthalimide fungicides widely used in agricultural and non-agricultural settings and have been identified as environmental risk factors for Parkinson's disease (PD). These pesticides are highly reactive with cellular thiols, particularly glutathione (GSH), disrupting redox homeostasis and inducing neuronal toxicity; however, the mechanisms underlying their neurotoxicity remain poorly understood. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by impaired antioxidant defenses, including GSH depletion and phospholipid peroxidation. This study examined whether captan and folpet induce or modulate ferroptosis in immortalized neuronal and non-neuronal cell lines. Cytotoxicity and intracellular GSH levels were assessed using calcein AM and monochlorobimane assays, respectively. Captan and folpet exhibited marked cytotoxicity in rat dopaminergic (N27) cells, with IC₅₀ values of 3.7 and 6.2 μM, respectively. Co-treatment with the thiol-containing compounds N-acetylcysteine and dithiothreitol markedly protected against toxicity induced by both pesticides, supporting thiol reactivity as an important mechanism underlying their toxicity. In addition, captan and folpet did not substantially induce ferroptotic cell death on their own; they significantly enhanced susceptibility to RSL3-induced ferroptotic stress while attenuating erastin-induced cytotoxicity. These differential effects may reflect the distinct mechanisms by which RSL3 and erastin initiate ferroptotic stress, together with the thiol-reactive properties of captan and folpet. Collectively, these findings identify context-dependent modulation of ferroptotic susceptibility as a previously unrecognized mechanism that may contribute to the cellular effects of these PD-associated pesticides.

title: Aged Extracellular Vesicles and Whole Serum Disrupt a Multicellular Human Blood-Brain Barrier Model Through Distinct Mechanisms.
journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
abstract: Age-associated changes in circulating factors contribute to blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, yet the relative effects of serum and serum-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) remain unclear. Here, we used a human multicellular transwell BBB model, composed of primary brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs), astrocytes, pericytes, and neural progenitor cells (hNPCs) derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), to compare the effects of serum and serum-derived EVs from young-adult and aged mice on BBB integrity. Barrier function was assessed by transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER) and permeability to 3-5 and 40 kDa FITC-dextran, and cellular organization and junctional integrity were evaluated by immunofluorescence. Although TEER exhibited treatment-dependent differences, permeability assays revealed distinct age- and treatment-associated changes in macromolecular transport. Aged EVs increased permeability to both dextran tracers relative to young EVs and markedly reduced ZO-1 coverage, whereas aged serum produced the greatest permeability to the 40 kDa tracer and the most pronounced loss of BMEC alignment. These changes occurred without a significant reduction in overall vWF-positive endothelial area, indicating structural and functional remodeling rather than overt endothelial loss. Additionally, young serum increased TUJ1-positive area and claudin-5 coverage, pointing to broader cell-type-specific effects. Together, these findings show that aging shifted the BBB toward greater macromolecular permeability and poorer endothelial organization, with aged EVs acting primarily on junctional integrity and aged serum driving the larger increase in permeability and loss of endothelial alignment.

title: Smartphone-Based Passive Sensing Improves Measurement-Based Pharmacological Interventions in Depression.
Single-Nucleus RNA Sequencing Identifies MBOAT1 Governs Schwann Cell Senescence Through the cGAS-STING-p-TBK1 Signaling Axis in the Aging Peripheral Nerve.
abstract: Peripheral nerve aging is a progressive decline that leads to sensorimotor deficits, decreased nerve conduction velocity, and compromised regenerative capacity in the elderly. Although it directly precipitates sensory ataxia and chronic neuropathic pain, the cell-autonomous mechanisms governing peripheral nerve aging remain largely elusive. In this study, we employed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to profile the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) and sciatic nerve tissues of adult and aged rats. Our findings indicate that the cellular composition and gene expression of the dorsal root ganglion in adult rats differ significantly from those in aged rats, as do the cellular composition and gene expression of the sciatic nerve. Notably, we identified that Mboat1 regulates the cGAS-STING signaling pathway; its age-induced dysregulation triggers Schwann cell senescence and drives peripheral nerve degeneration. Collectively, our study provides a novel molecular mechanism underlying peripheral nerve aging and highlights the Mboat1/cGAS-STING axis as a potential therapeutic target for age-related neuropathies.

title: Nociceptive thresholds and beta-endorphin concentrations in horses with pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction: a cross-sectional comparative study.
abstract: Increased beta-endorphin (β-END) concentrations in horses with pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID) are hypothesized to lead to increased pain tolerance of affected horses, however, alteration of nociceptive thresholds (NTs) in PPID horses has not been investigated previously. Evaluate whether NTs differ between horses with PPID and controls and whether β-END concentrations correlate with NTs. Fifty equids aged 19-32 years. Cross-sectional comparative study conducted in February 2025. The study included a PPID group (n = 24 horses) and a control group (n = 26 horses). Both groups were subjected to mechanical and thermal stimulation, and NTs were recorded. Plasma adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and β-END concentrations were quantified, and the association between β-END concentrations and NTs was analyzed. Although β-END concentrations were higher in the PPID group (482 [316-735] pg/mL [geometric mean (95% confidence interval [CI])]) compared with controls (47.8 [23.0-53.4] pg/mL [geometric mean (95% CI)]; P < .001), no correlation between β-END concentrations and NTs was found. Furthermore, no significant group differences and correlations were found for mechanical (MNTs) and thermal nociceptive thresholds (TNTs). In this selected cohort of older horses without clinically relevant pain, horses with PPID did not exhibit increased NTs compared to controls. Although β-END concentrations were higher in horses with PPID, no association between β-END concentrations and NTs was identified. These findings do not support a measurable effect of increased circulating β-END concentrations on NTs in the study cohort.

title: Decreased astrocytic CCL5 by Mir324 ameliorates ischemic stroke injury via the CCR5/ERK/CREB pathway.
abstract: Following ischemic stroke, Ccl5 mRNA expression increased, while Mir324 expression decreased in the peri-infarct cortex of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice. However, the roles of CCL5 and Mir324 in stroke remained largely unclear. Here, we show that inhibiting CCL5 using antibodies or Mir324 not only reduced infarct area and preserved neurological function in MCAO mice but also attenuated astrocyte reactivity and microglial activation, protected dendritic structures, and maintained spine density. In an astrocyte-neuron co-culture system after oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), inhibiting astrocytic CCL5 by antibody or Mir324 decreased neuronal apoptosis and preserved dendritic structure. Importantly, the suppression of CCL5 enhanced ERK/CREB pathway signaling both in vivo and in vitro. Consistent with these findings, the application of Maraviroc, a CCR5 antagonist, reduced infarct size, decreased neuronal apoptosis, and upregulated the ERK/CREB pathway in neurons treated with OGD. In conclusion, targeting the CCL5 pathway via Mir324 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for alleviating ischemic stroke damage through modulation of the neuronal CCR5/ERK/CREB pathway.

title: Immediate Postpartum Mental Health and Sleep in Mothers and Fathers with Healthy Newborns.
abstract: The postpartum period represents a critical window for parental psychological adjustment, but whether this is the case immediately after birth remains understudied. Furthermore, while many aspects of maternal mental health have been widely investigated in high-risk contexts, less is known about critical factors such as sleep-related vulnerability and attachment-related processes in low-risk situations, how these relate to early mental health in fathers, or how these factors may be associated with neonatal behavior. Thirty-two mother-father-newborn triads, comprising 32 mothers, 32 fathers, and their 32 healthy, full-term newborns, were included in the study. Newborn behavioral functioning was evaluated with the NBAS on Day 2. Mothers completed the EPDS, ECR, and STAI on Day 3. Both parents completed the CES-D, PSS, SCI, and FIRST on Day 3. Correlation, paired-comparison, and exploratory regression analyses were conducted. Clinically relevant elevations on at least one psychological or sleep-related measure were observed in 59.4% of mothers and 28.1% of fathers. Mothers showed significantly higher depressive symptoms, poorer sleep quality, and greater sleep reactivity than fathers. Among mothers, depressive symptoms were associated with greater sleep reactivity, with trait anxiety showing the strongest association with depressive symptoms. Maternal and paternal depressive symptoms were also positively associated across partners. Newborn behavioral functioning was broadly within expected ranges, and no association between parental psychological or sleep-related measures and NBAS cluster scores survived FDR correction. Psychological and sleep-related vulnerability was detectable in parents during the immediate postpartum period in this low-risk clinical context, with higher levels observed in mothers. Cross-partner concordance was limited to depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that early screening of both parents may be clinically relevant. Sleep reactivity and anxiety were associated with maternal postpartum distress, but their potential predictive value requires confirmation in longitudinal studies.

title: Do Interindividual Differences Matter? Testing Differences in Locus Coeruleus MRI Contrast as a Function of Age, Sex, and Body Mass Index.
abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) plays a key role in cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Investigating demographic differences in the LC is important because these differences may contribute to lifelong AD risk. Noninvasive MRI assessments of LC contrast are associated with cognitive performance and are hypothesized to reflect the nucleus's structural integrity. Age and sex differences in LC MRI contrast have been documented. Nonetheless, results are mixed, and most previous studies are hampered by small samples and a lack of standardization in the inspection of data quality and registration accuracy. In this cross-sectional study, we aim to investigate differences in LC MRI contrast as a function of demographic variables associated with increased AD prevalence: age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). We will pool fast spin echo (FSE) scans of young (age: 18-33) and older adults (age: 55-90) from eight datasets collected in three sites (N = 663). A semiautomatic pipeline will be adopted to register FSE scans to MNI space and segment the LC using a high-confidence LC mask. To maximize reproducibility, we will evaluate data quality using markers of in-scanner motion and nonphysiological noise, and we will rely on a standardized visual inspection to assess registration accuracy. We will run linear mixed models, including a nested random effect of acquisition batch (i.e., datasets grouped by study and site) to account for variability in LC MRI contrast driven by non-biological factors (e.g., hardware). We expect that LC contrast is positively associated with chronological age in young adults but negatively associated in older adults. On average, it is expected to be higher in older adults and in females. We will explore sex-by-age-group effects and BMI differences in LC MRI contrast. This study offers a reproducible foundation for understanding demographic variation in LC MRI contrast.

title: Sex differences in neural activity across amygdalo-striatal network during social behaviour.
abstract: Social behaviour is essential for the survival of most mammalian species and is shaped by sex-dependent genetic and endocrine factors. However, how sex influences brain-wide neural dynamics during social interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated sex differences in neural activity across a distributed amygdalo-striatal network in freely behaving mice. Using chronically implanted electrode arrays, we simultaneously recorded extracellular activity from multiple amygdalo-striatal regions while mice performed four social discrimination tasks. Neural signals were analysed alongside video-based behavioural tracking and head acceleration measurements. We identified significant sex differences in neural activity that emerged even before social interaction, suggesting distinct anticipatory network states. During social interaction, sex differences were distributed across brain regions and electrophysiological features, but were most consistently expressed in the basolateral amygdala (BLA). Notably, BLA activity exhibited pronounced sex-specific, context- and time-dependent dynamics, particularly during the initial phase of social interaction. These neural differences were associated with variations in behavioural responses and movement dynamics. Together, our findings reveal that sex shapes both baseline and interaction-driven neural activity across the social brain network, and highlight the BLA as a key node underlying sex-specific dynamics of social behaviour.

title: Mesenchymal stromal cells for periventricular hemorrhagic infarction in extremely preterm infants: a double-blinded randomized controlled phase IIa clinical trial.
abstract: Periventricular hemorrhagic infarction in extremely preterm infants (PVHI; the most severe form of intraventricular hemorrhage) are associated with a high risk of mortality and neurodevelopmental disability with no effective treatments. We aimed to assess the safety and potential efficacy of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) for PVHI in preterm infants. We conducted a single-center, phase 2a double-blind randomized controlled trial at the Samsung Medical Center. Twenty-two preterm infants (23-31 weeks gestation) with PVHI were double-blindly randomized (1:1) to receive intraventricular MSCs (1 × 107 cells/kg) or normal saline within 7 days post-diagnosis. Primary outcome was combined rate of ventriculo-peritoneal shunt or death. Secondary outcomes included safety, mortality, cerebral palsy (CP), epilepsy, developmental delays. The primary endpoint of shunt or death by 36 weeks' postmenstrual age did not differ between groups (relative risk 1.14, 95% CI 0.64 to 2.03). Among survivors assessed through 2 years' corrected age, the MSC group had lower observed rates of cerebral palsy, epilepsy, and microcephaly than the placebo group, although confidence intervals were wide; lower incidence of CP (relative risk 0.56, 95% CI 0.27 to 1.17), epilepsy (relative risk 0.38, 95% CI 0.10 to 1.36) and microcephaly (relative risk 0.30, 95% CI 0.08 to 1.07). No serious treatment-related adverse events occurred. Intraventricular MSC therapy did not reduce the mortality or VP shunting dependence in premature infants with PVHI. However, 2-year exploratory long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes suggested potential benefits, which warranting confirmation in larger trials. Trial registration The study protocol was registered at Clinical Trials.gov (NCT02890953) on September 6, 2016.

title: Comparative study of BBB-crossing AAV capsids for central nervous system delivery efficiency.
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) severely restricts the efficacy of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Here, we systematically characterized the in vivo tissue distribution and expression patterns of three BBB-crossing AAV capsids (PHP.eB, CNSRCV300, BI-hTFR1) after intravenous delivery in mice, using the ubiquitous CAG promoter and neuron-specific hSyn promoter to drive reporter expression. Compared with conventional AAV9, PHP.eB and CNSRCV300 exhibited enhanced BBB penetration and brain transduction, with predominant neuronal tropism. Relative to the CAG promoter, hSyn slightly attenuated cerebral transgene expression and markedly diminished peripheral off-target expression. Nevertheless, immunofluorescence, qPCR and Western blot assays verified persistent AAV retention in peripheral tissues including the liver, indicating underlying safety hazards. Notably, CNSRCV300 achieved robust CNS transduction with minimal peripheral accumulation, conferring superior safety profiles and promising clinical potential. Collectively, AAV in vivo targeting is co-regulated by capsid variants and promoter characteristics. Neuronal-specific promoters efficiently mitigate peripheral off-target transgene expression but fail to eliminate residual peripheral viral deposition, a critical safety concern for systemic AAV therapy. This study provides systematic experimental evidence for the rational screening and optimization of CNS-targeted AAV vectors.

title: A hub-and-spoke network organizational model in Liguria (Italy) for managing anaphylaxis in pediatric age: a retrospective analysis.
abstract: Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction for which intramuscular epinephrine is the sole non-deferrable first-line treatment. Despite well-established international guidelines, real-world adherence remains critically suboptimal, particularly in peripheral emergency settings. This study examines anaphylaxis management in children aged 0-16 years presenting to the emergency department within the Gaslini Diffuso initiative, a structured Hub-and-Spoke pediatric network in Liguria, Italy, to evaluate inter-institutional variability in clinical practice. We conducted a multicenter retrospective observational study spanning 10 years at the Hub Center (IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini, Genoa; January 2013 - December 2023) and 2 years across all network centers (January 2022 - December 2023). Anaphylaxis was defined according to the NIAID/FAAN 2006 criteria. The cohort comprised 168 patients aged 0-16 years, distributed across the Hub Center and four Spoke Centers. Epinephrine was administered in only 34.9% of patients overall (rising to 52.8% in the 2022-2023 period), with marked inter-institutional variability across the network (Hub 52.8% vs. La Spezia 6.7%). Antihistamines (89.2%) and corticosteroids (87.3%) dominated clinical practice despite lacking proven efficacy in preventing anaphylaxis progression. Tryptase measurement was performed in 43.4% (acute) and 21.1% (baseline) of Hub patients. Autoinjector prescription was documented in only 26.5% of newly eligible patients, and as low as 5.3% at Savona-Pietra Ligure. These findings suggest significant gaps that may contribute to suboptimal outcomes, underscoring the urgent need for network-wide epinephrine-first protocols and structured training programs.

title: A conditional Vrk1 cholinergic knockout mouse recapitulates severe human motor neuron disease.
abstract: Mutations in the VRK1 (Vaccinia-related kinase 1) gene have been implicated in neurodegenerative disease, primarily affecting motor neurons (MNs) and brain development. However, VRK1's role in MN function and underlying disease mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated VRK1's role in motor neuron disease (MND) by generating a conditional knockout (cKO) mouse model lacking Vrk1 in cholinergic neurons. We created a Vrk1-targeted Cre-lox MND mouse model, in which Cre recombination resulted in a null mutation of Vrk1. Cre-recombinase was expressed in cholinergic neurons, including MNs, generating a cholinergic neuron-specific Vrk1 KO mouse (Vrk1 ChAT-cKO). The phenotype was analyzed by observation and motor testing; MN degeneration, neuromuscular junction (NMJ) denervation, and muscle atrophy were assessed using histological and immunostaining techniques. Vrk1 ChAT-cKO mice showed progressive motor degeneration, including weight loss, reduced grip strength, tail dragging, decreased mobility, tremors, kyphosis, and respiratory distress, leading to premature death by approximately 27 days. Histological analysis of spinal cord sections from postnatal day 24-27 cKO mice revealed significant MN degeneration, including vacuolation, chromatolysis, apoptosis and neuroinflammation, with a 40-50% loss of ChAT positive MNs. Remaining MNs exhibited a 36-44% reduction in mean soma size. NMJ analysis showed 60% denervation and abnormal postsynaptic AChR cluster maturation. Muscle histology revealed nearly 79% reduction in myofiber area. The Vrk1 ChAT-cKO mouse model recapitulates the severe MN phenotype observed in human VRK1-related neurodegeneration, underscoring VRK1's critical role in MN integrity. The progressive motor dysfunction, NMJ abnormalities and muscle atrophy, suggest that VRK1 is essential for MN survival and neuromuscular functions. This model offers a valuable tool for studying VRK1-associated MND and could contribute to the development and assessment of therapeutic strategies targeting VRK1 pathways. Additionally, it may provide insights into shared mechanisms between other MNDs, such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

title: Characteristics of ischemic stroke patients with left atrial appendage thrombus detected by cardiac photon-counting detector computed tomography.
abstract: The early identification of left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) or transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients can have relevant treatment and prognostic implications. We investigated the prevalence of LAA thrombus in AIS/TIA patients and analyzed baseline characteristics and short-term outcomes according to the presence of LAA thrombus. We analyzed stroke patients who were admitted consecutively in our comprehensive stroke centre between March 2023 and December 2025 and received cardiac photon-counting computed tomography (CT) implemented in the acute stroke imaging protocol. We analyzed baseline clinical characteristics, echocardiographic and laboratory biomarkers, in-hospital mortality and in-hospital ischemic stroke recurrence according to the presence of LAA thrombus. We included 577 patients with a median age of 75 years, 49.6% were female, and LAA thrombus was found in 49 patients (8.5%). The presence of LAA thrombus was independently associated with atrial fibrillation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 16.09, 95% confidence interval [95%CI] = 4.55-56.90, p < 0.001), severe left atrial dilatation (aOR = 3.48, 95%CI = 1.18-10.26, p = 0.009) and higher NT-proBNP (aOR per 1000pg/mL-increment = 1.10, 95%CI = 1.01-1.19, p = 0.022). In-hospital mortality was higher in patients with LAA thrombus (p = 0.003), but this association did not persist after adjustment for clinical stroke severity. In-hospital ischemic stroke recurrence was similar in both groups. Stroke patients with LAA thrombus detected on cardiac CT performed as part of the acute stroke imaging protocol have different baseline characteristics which are indicative of more severe underlying atrial substrate for arrhythmogenesis.

title: Nsun5 deficiency leads to impaired myelin integrity and sleep disruption.
abstract: Sleep disruption is common in disorders involving white-matter abnormalities, but the molecular pathways linking ribosomal RNA modification to disordered sleep remain unclear. NSUN5, which encodes an rRNA methyltransferase, is deleted in most patients with Williams-Beuren syndrome (WBS), a condition frequently accompanied by sleep problems. This clinical association suggests that loss of NSUN5 may contribute to sleep dysfunction, potentially through mechanisms relevant to white-matter integrity and neural activity. We combined electroencephalography/electromyography phenotyping, transcriptomics, ribosome profiling, nascent proteomics, proteomics, electron microscopy, positron emission tomography-computed tomography, and pharmacological rescue experiments in Nsun5-knockout mice to define how loss of Nsun5-dependent 28 S ribosomal RNA 5-methylcytosine affects white-matter integrity and sleep. Nsun5 deficiency markedly reduced 28 S rRNA m5C levels and led to selective translational dysregulation rather than global translational failure. The affected translational programs were enriched in myelination-related pathways and voltage-gated potassium channel subunits, including Kcna1 and Kcna2. At the cellular and tissue levels, these alterations were associated with oligodendrocyte loss, diffuse hypomyelination of the corpus callosum, and increased regional cortical metabolic activity. Correspondingly, Nsun5-knockout mice exhibited reduced non-rapid-eye-movement sleep and altered nocturnal sleep organization. Treatment with clemastine significantly improved sleep abnormalities and restored myelin integrity, while treatment with 4-aminopyridine also alleviated the sleep phenotype. These findings suggest that Nsun5-dependent rRNA methylation contributes to sleep disruption in association with white-matter dysfunction and altered potassium-channel-related protein abundance. Our results provide a preclinical framework for understanding sleep disturbances associated with WBS and other myelin-related neurological conditions.

title: Effects of caffeine ingestion on outdoor 800-m running performance: a randomized controlled crossover study with hierarchical regression analysis.
abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated that caffeine ingestion improves simulated 800-m run performance; however, whether caffeine enhances 800-m performance during outdoor track running, in which environmental conditions may influence performance, remains unclear. Furthermore, it also remains unclear whether caffeine ingestion affects arterial oxygen saturation during 800-m outdoor running. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the effects of caffeine ingestion on outdoor 800-m run performance and physiological responses. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study, 14 (4 females) college middle-distance runners with an 800-m seasonal best of 128.48 ± 14.11 s ingested capsules containing either (1) placebo or (2) caffeine (6 mg/kg of body weight). Following ingestion, they performed an 800-m run on an outdoor track. To ensure consistency in pacing strategy between trials, pacemakers were employed until the 400-m mark. The first 200 m was run at 103% of the average speed calculated from each participant's seasonal-best 800-m time, followed by 200 m at 97% of that speed, as the initial 200 m of an 800-m race is typically faster than the rest of the pace. The placebo and caffeine trials recorded similar running times (134.8 ± 15.1 vs 135.1 ± 15.3 s, P = 0.602). Furthermore, arterial oxygen saturation, heart rate, peak blood lactate concentration, and rating of perceived exertion were comparable between the trials. Air temperature during the run tended to be lower (17.1 ± 3.4 vs 19.2 ± 2.8 °C, P = 0.062), and the wind speed tended to be greater (2.0 ± 1.2 vs 1.2 ± 0.8 m/s, P = 0.051) in the caffeine than in the placebo trial. Hierarchical multiple regression analysis revealed that adding caffeine ingestion to a baseline model including environmental factors significantly improved the model fit (ΔR2 = 0.10, P = 0.039). After adjusting wind speed and air temperature, caffeine ingestion was associated with faster 800-m running time (B = - 11.58, P = 0.039). These findings suggest that caffeine ingestion was associated with faster outdoor 800-m running time after accounting for environmental conditions.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome in the context of venlafaxine and tamoxifen: a case report.
abstract: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is classically associated with potent dopamine D2 receptor blockade from antipsychotic medications. Emerging evidence, however, suggests that non-neuroleptic agents may also precipitate NMS by destabilizing dopaminergic pathways. We report a case highlighting the potential role of tamoxifen and venlafaxine in lowering the threshold for NMS through convergent neuroendocrine and monoaminergic effects. We describe a 68-year-old white American female who developed NMS in the setting of polypharmacy, including tamoxifen and venlafaxine, and pair this with a mechanistic analysis of how these medications may meaningfully lower the threshold for NMS. We propose that endocrine disruption, serotonergic-noradrenergic modulation, and cumulative dopaminergic burden converge to produce a state of dopaminergic instability that predisposes susceptible patients to NMS, even in the absence of high-potency dopamine antagonists. Recognition of tamoxifen and venlafaxine as potential contributors to dopaminergic instability expands the conceptual framework of NMS beyond traditional high-potency neuroleptic-centric models. Increased awareness of these underappreciated pharmacologic risk factors may improve diagnostic clarity, facilitate earlier recognition of atypical NMS presentations, and inform safer prescribing and monitoring strategies for high-risk individuals.

title: Identification of phenotypic abnormalities and effector function impairment in natural killer cells of patients with ataxia-telangiectasia.
abstract: Ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T) is a rare inherited disorder resulting from mutations in the ATM gene and characterized by progressive neurodegeneration, immunological abnormalities, and increased infection and cancer susceptibility. There is no cure for A-T, and life expectancy is drastically reduced because of pulmonary disease and cancer. Humoral or T/B-cell deficiency was associated with reduced survival in A-T patients, although the findings remain controversial. Conversely, A-T patients display normal numbers of NK cells, crucial components of the antitumor and antiviral innate immunity. The goal of the present study was to investigate the function of NK cells in A-T. Peripheral blood NK cells of 31 A-T patients were analyzed via flow cytometry to assess their distribution across subpopulations and expression of maturation markers, receptors and effector molecules. Additionally, we assessed the capacity of NK cells to kill K562 cells and to produce IFN-γ in response to IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 stimulation. The plasma levels of soluble ligands for the NKG2D receptor (sNKG2DLs) and cytokines were measured via ELISA. Compared with control NK cells, A-T patient NK cells presented higher frequencies of the CD56bright and CD56dimCD16- subsets and contraction of the highly cytotoxic CD56dim subset that, however, showed a normal maturation pattern. The expression of the main activating/inhibitory receptors was conserved on A-T NK cells, except for the up- and downregulation of PD-1 and NKG2D, respectively. NKG2D downregulation correlated with accumulation of the sNKG2DLs sMICA and sULBP2 in patient plasma. Importantly, A-T NK cells were inefficient at producing IFN-γ upon stimulation and strongly impaired at killing tumor targets, dysfunctions that were reproduced by inhibiting ATM in PBMCs of healthy individuals. Finally, in A-T plasma, we detected elevated levels of IL-6, which correlated with NK-cell phenotypic alterations and reduced IFN-γ response, and increased levels of TGF-β, which correlated with impaired NK-cell cytotoxicity. The present study fills a gap in the field of A-T immunity, revealing exhaustion-associated features and functional impairment of NK cells correlated with increased plasma concentrations of sNKG2DLs and the immunosuppressive cytokines IL-6 and TGF-β. These findings indicate that NK defects can contribute to cancer and infection susceptibility and provide hints for improving current therapies for A-T.
keywords: NK Cell Lectin-Like Receptor Subfamily K

title: Predictors and prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19: a prospective observational study.
abstract: Dysfunctional breathing is increasingly recognised among individuals with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), yet data on long-term prevalence and predictors are scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing, as indicated by elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, four years after COVID-19 illness in adults with PCC and identified associated factors and baseline predictors by comparing individuals with and without elevated NQ scores. In this prospective observational study, adults with PCC, both previously hospitalised and non-hospitalised for COVID-19, were recruited from a specialised post-COVID outpatient clinic. Baseline assessments (2020-2022) were analysed together with data from a digital follow-up survey in 2024. Symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing was defined as a NQ score ≥ 23 at follow-up. Between group differences were examined, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors and baseline predictors. Among 288 participants (median follow-up 50 months), 143 (50%) had symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing. These individuals were younger, often female, and more frequently non-hospitalised during acute COVID-19. Baseline predictors included non-hospitalisation, higher dyspnoea severity, lower FEV1, and younger age. At four years, elevated NQ scores (≥ 23) were independently associated with higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Individuals with symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing performed worse in the six-minute walk test, one-minute sit to stand test, and maximal inspiratory pressure test at baseline, whereas lung function did not differ. Patient-reported outcomes were consistently worse compared with those with NQ scores < 23 and improved less over time. Half of the individuals with PCC in this cohort reported symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19, as indicated by a NQ score ≥ 23. Elevated NQ scores were associated with greater PCC-symptom burden and poorer health outcomes, highlighting their potential clinical relevance in long-term PCC. Future studies should combine patient-reported measures with objective assessment of breathing pattern and ventilatory function.

title: Non-invasive in vivo imaging assessment of retinal microglia-like cells in diabetic retinopathy by adaptive optics optical coherence tomography.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a microvascular, neurodegenerative and inflammatory disorder characterised by retinal microglial activation. In this study, we used adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) to assess microglia-like cell morphology and density at the inner limiting membrane (ILM) in vivo in eyes with DR and healthy controls. Eleven eyes from nine patients with DR and seven eyes from seven healthy controls were examined using a prototype AO-OCT system. Volumetric images were acquired over a 4°×4° field of view at five standardised retinal locations extending from the superior vascular arcade to the parafovea. For ultrastructural reference, a retinal sample from the foveal region of a 51-year-old donor was analysed using serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBFSEM). Retinal microglia-like cells were consistently visualised at the ILM in all participants using single-volume AO-OCT imaging. High-resolution imaging allowed identification of distinct morphological phenotypes consistent with histological findings and SBFSEM observations. The proportion of cells with a reactive morphology was higher in eyes with DR than in controls (median 51% vs. 16%). Overall cell density did not differ significantly between groups but showed considerable interindividual variability. In contrast, a greater proportion of cells were embedded within the ILM in DR eyes compared with controls (median 90% vs. 53%). SBFSEM provided detailed ultrastructural characterisation, revealing fine processes approximately 100-400 nm in diameter extending from the soma of microglia with a reactive morphology, a feature not previously reported. AO-OCT enables three-dimensional, quantitative assessment of microglia-like cell morphology and distribution in healthy eyes and eyes with DR. Eyes with DR showed an increased proportion of cells with a reactive morphology and a greater proportion of cells embedded within the ILM, suggesting increased retinal immune activation. These findings support AO-OCT as a tool for investigating retinal inflammatory changes in DR and other retinal disorders.

title: Anacyclus pyrethrum extract improves spatial memory and cognition in a rat model of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most prevalent dementia disorder, causing significant disability in the affected patients. This disorder is currently considered incurable. In this study, we aim to use the hydroalcoholic extract of Anacyclus Pyrethrum (AP) as a potential treatment for cognitive dysfunction in a rat model of AD induced with intracerebroventricular injection of Amyloid-beta 1-42. Forty-eight rats were randomly assigned to six groups (n = 8): control, sham, Aβ-injected (5 µg, ICV), and treatment groups receiving AP extract (500 mg/kg/day), donepezil (0.3 mg/kg/day), or their combination for 14 days following AD induction. Spatial memory was assessed using the Morris Water Maze (MWM), and brain metabolic changes were evaluated using positron emission tomography (PET). Histopathological analyses were also performed. Positron emission tomography (PET) scan results supported the successful induction of Aβ‑related metabolic changes. MWM results showed that treatment groups significantly decreased swim distance to the platform, increased time spent in the target quadrant, and reduced mean distance from the former platform location. AP-treated, donepezil, and combination therapies demonstrated significantly better performance over time. Oral administration of the hydroalcoholic extract of AP was associated with improved memory performance in a rat model of AD. These results call for more research to assess the AP extract's ability to reduce cognitive impairments in AD.

title: Exploring white matter integrity in major depressive disorder with and without suicidal attempts: a diffusion tensor imaging study.
abstract: The study investigates the neurobiological basis of suicidality in patients with Major Depressive Disorder with suicidal attempts (MDD + SA) by examining differences in white matter integrity among three groups: MDD + SA, MDD-SA without suicide attempts, and healthy controls (HC). Sixty-one participants-17 with MDD + SA, 19 MDD-SA, and 25 HC-underwent diffusion MRI scans to assess white matter microstructure using measures such as fractional anisotropy (FA), axial diffusivity (AD), radial diffusivity (RD), and mean diffusivity (MD). Correlational tractography was then performed to identify white matter pathways affected in suicidality. Compared to patients with MDD-SA, patients with MDD + SA exhibited distinct bilateral white matter microstructural changes. They showed greater FA and AD in the cingulum tracts, including the bilateral Cingulum Frontal Parietal, bilateral Cingulum Frontal Parahippocampal, and right Cingulum Parolfactory, as well as higher FA in the left Cingulum Parolfactory. Furthermore, patients with MDD + SA showed lower MD and RD in the right Cingulum Frontal Parietal and right Cingulum Parolfactory, and lower RD in the bilateral Cingulum Frontal Parahippocampal and left Cingulum Parolfactory, compared to patients with MDD-SA. In contrast, patients with MDD + SA demonstrated lower FA in the right Frontal Corticopontine tract compared to MDD-SA. Relative to HC, patients with MDD + SA showed higher FA and lower RD across the cingulum bundle, including the bilateral Cingulum Frontal Parietal, bilateral Cingulum Parolfactory, and left Cingulum Frontal Parahippocampal. They also exhibited higher AD in the left Cingulum Frontal Parietal, left Cingulum Parolfactory, and left Cingulum Frontal Parahippocampal, as well as lower MD in the right Cingulum Frontal Parietal and right Cingulum Parolfactory compared to HC. In addition, patients with MDD + SA showed an interesting pattern of elevated FA with reduced MD, RD, and AD in the Corpus Callosum Forceps Major and lower FA in the Corpus Callosum Forceps Minor, compared to HC. These findings highlight specific white matter microstructural differences in MDD + SA, particularly in the cingulum bundle, which may serve as neurobiological markers of suicidality, potentially enabling more effective assessment and intervention techniques. Not applicable.

title: Public discourse towards volunteering in prisons: an infodemiology study of Twitter data.
abstract: Worldwide volunteering plays a key role in helping people in need. Volunteering in prisons contributes to the rehabilitation of inmates during their time in jail and their reintegration back in society. However, little is known about the general population's attitudes towards volunteering in prison. We conducted a content analysis of publicly available data on Twitter from 1st January 2017 to 31st October 2022. The codebook used consisted of classifying tweets according to the type of content and type of user. The number of retweets and likes generated by each tweet was analysed as an indicator of user interest; the type of content was investigated per continent; an emotion analysis was also conducted. A total of 101,349 tweets in English and 5,001 tweets in Portuguese were considered classifiable. 'Volunteering as an alternative to jail time or reduced sentence time' was the topic that generated most tweets and 'Volunteering impact' was the topic that generated the least in both languages. America was the continent with more tweets; in both languages, the average number of likes per tweet was higher than the average number of retweets. Angry emotions were the most expressed by users. This study is the first application of social media research to investigate the public discourse about volunteering in prisons. Overall, public attitudes towards volunteering in prisons are negative. Continued efforts are required to raise awareness about volunteering in prisons.

title: Association between beta-blocker selectivity and mortality in left heart failure patients with comorbid COPD.
abstract: To evaluate the Impact of posterior to intensive care unit (ICU) beta-blockers use with the clinical outcomes in patients with left heart failure(LHF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease(COPD). Patients with LHF and COPD were selected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV(MIMIC-IV) database for this retrospective observational study. The primary outcome was 30-day and 365-day all-cause mortality. Comparative survival analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier estimators to evaluate mortality rates among HF and COPD patients. Hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated to determine the association between post-ICU beta-blockers users and prognosis using Cox proportional hazard models. A total of 3255 patients with LHF complicated by COPD were finally selected. Among them, 2740 patients (84.18%) were treated with beta-blockers, including 1963 patients (60.31%) treated with cardio-selective beta-blockers and 777 patients (23.87%) treated with non-cardio-selective beta-blockers. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed that the 30-day(HR:0.291;95%CI:0.236-0.357; P 0.05). Our study demonstrates that beta-blockers significantly reduce all-cause mortality in patients with LHF and COPD, an effect particularly associated with non-cardioselective agents. Interestingly, this benefit may depend more on drug class (selectivity) than on dosing intensity.

title: Aerobic exercise inhibits lung adenocarcinoma invasion dependent on the superior cervical ganglion.
abstract: To elucidate possible neural and molecular pathway mechanisms underlying the suppression of aerobic exercise in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) invasion. Sympathetic nerve distribution was visualized via immunofluorescent staining in human tissue microarrays (TMAs) and mouse lung specimens. Pseudorabies virus (PRV) retrograde tracing method was employed to identify the brain-lung neural circuit, and superior cervical ganglionectomy was administrated to achieve pulmonary sympathetic denervation. Voluntary wheel running (VWR) worked as an aerobic exercise to intervene the brain-lung neural circuit to suppress mouse LUAD invasion. Norepinephrine (NE) levels and the expression of ADRB2 and MMP2 were assessed using ELISA, Western blot and qRT-PCR methods. RNA sequencing, along with transwell and wound-healing assays, were conducted on lentiviral-mediated ADRB2-overexpressing LUAD cells to evaluate migratory and invasive behaviors. Substantial sympathetic nerve infiltration was detected in both human and mouse LUAD specimens, with a negative correlation observed between intratumoral sympathetic nerve density and tumor volume. Retrograde tracing revealed that pulmonary sympathetic nerves are predominantly innervated by the superior cervical ganglion (SCG). SCG resection abrogated the exercise-induced elevation in intratumoral NE and reversed the anti-invasion benefits of exercise. In vitro, NE treatment downregulated MMP2 expression and impaired the migration and invasion of LUAD cells. Similarly, ADRB2 overexpression suppresses LUAD invasion by inhibiting MMP2 expression. The SCG acts as a relay hub connecting higher brain centers to intratumoral sympathetic activity, and VWR engages this SCG-mediated pathway to exert an anti-invasive effect on LUAD invasion. VWR stimulates NE release from intratumoral sympathetic nerves in LUAD. NE inhibits LUAD invasion via the ADRB2-MMP2 signaling pathway.

title: Beyond coercion: developing post-coercive practice support for mental health inpatients, a modified e-Delphi consensus process.
abstract: Exposure to coercive practices in mental healthcare is associated with a range of patient harms. Clinical guidelines recommend that patients exposed to coercive practice in inpatient settings are offered support, however, existing post-coercive practice support models are often limited to debrief approaches, lack clear operationalisation, and have not integrated lived experience perspectives in their design. There remains a lack of clarity regarding the aims, optimal delivery approaches, core components and preferred personnel of such interventions. This consultation therefore aimed to determine areas of consensus and disagreement on the components and structure of a post-coercive practice support intervention for mental health inpatients. A consultation employing a three-round modified e-Delphi process was conducted with an expert panel of patients, family/carers, and mental health staff in the United Kingdom. Survey items comprised aims, delivery approaches, components and personnel for a patient post-coercive practice support intervention. In Round 1 experts rated importance of components; in Round 2 items were sequenced across three time points (immediate, intermediate and post-discharge); and in Round 3 the experts finalised a component checklist. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, while qualitative data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Consensus was defined a priori as agreement among ≥ 75% of the panel. Triangulation of quantitative and qualitative findings informed the final component checklist. Consensus was reached on 39 intervention components. Following triangulation, a phased support framework was developed comprising 30 components in an immediate support phase, 18 in a later intermediate inpatient phase, and 4 in a post-discharge phase. Findings indicate distinct aims and components across the phases. In the early support phase patient safety and psychological stabilisation were prioritised. In the intermediate phase sharing of perspectives, mutual understanding and prevention of further coercive practice were prioritised. Consensus regarding the post-discharge phase was more limited and consequently remains underdeveloped. Findings suggest post-coercive practice support should be conceptualised as a multi-phase process rather than a singular debrief intervention. The resulting lived-experience-informed component checklist provides a framework for the operationalisation and feasibility testing of an inpatient post-coercive practice support intervention.

title: Marked dopaminergic denervation in early stages of Perry syndrome.
abstract: Perry Syndrome (PS) is a rare autosomal dominant disease caused by mutations in the DCTN1 gene. Clinically it is characterized by a combination of parkinsonism, neuropsychiatric symptoms, weight loss, and central hypoventilation. PS patients exhibit a variable response to dopaminergic medications. Dopaminergic imaging in these patients is rarely reported, but signs of presynaptic dopaminergic deficit are expected. We report a 43-year-old male with genetically confirmed PS who presented with early parkinsonism and relatively preserved response to levodopa, and before developing respiratory problems and weight loss. Ioflupane I-123 SPECT (DaTSCAN) repeatedly demonstrated nearly complete absence of striatal tracer uptake, a severity not previously described in early stages of the disease. This finding suggests that marked dopaminergic denervation may be present at an early clinical stage of Perry syndrome, even in patients who respond to levodopa. Whether this reflects dopaminergic involvement preceding more widespread neurodegeneration in the globus pallidus cannot be determined from a single case, and this possibility needs to be confirmed in larger studies.

title: KCNQ2 p.(Arg214Trp): systematic review with retrospective analysis and expanding the phenotype.
abstract: Heterozygous pathogenic variants in the KCNQ2 gene underlie a broad phenotypic spectrum ranging from self-limited (familial) neonatal epilepsy (SeLNE) to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy or isolated intellectual disability. The KCNQ2 gene encodes subunits of a voltage-gated potassium channel involved in neuronal excitability, and its mutations are known to have both loss-of-function (LoF) and gain-of-function (GoF) effects, resulting in distinct neurological syndromes. The recurrent missense LoF variant KCNQ2 p.(Arg214Trp) has been previously reported in a single family with a presumed SeLNE phenotype, without detailed adult follow-up and with additional database-reported evidence suggesting a broader phenotype associated with this recurrent variant. Here, we report a family with two adult carriers of the heterozygous KCNQ2 p.(Arg214Trp) variant identified through whole-exome sequencing, including long-term follow-up into late adulthood. In addition, a literature review of previously reported cases carrying the same recurrent variant was performed. Both individuals presented with early-onset focal epilepsy with a relapsing course, characterized by prolonged seizure-free periods followed by recurrence in adulthood. The proband demonstrated transient motor regression, developmental delay, moderate intellectual disability, ataxia and fine motor impairment. The father exhibited milder cognitive impairment and additional comorbidities in later life. These findings challenge the concept of KCNQ2 p.(Arg214Trp) as a self-limited epilepsy-associated variant and indicate a broader phenotypic spectrum, with persistence of epilepsy and associated neurological and non-neurological comorbidities into adulthood. Our report provides new insights into adult outcomes, aiding in genetic counseling and the long-term management of affected individuals. More extensive studies with larger cohorts carrying this variant are necessary to better define the full phenotypic spectrum and to distinguish comorbidities associated with different etiological factors, including perinatal factors.

title: Multidisciplinary prognostic accuracy in severe frailty: assessing short-term survival predictions in hospitalized older adults.
abstract: The increasing number of hospitalized older adults with severe frailty and limited life expectancy highlights the need for accurate short-term prognosis to inform care planning, effective communication, and resource allocation. However, survival prediction in this population is underexplored. This study aimed to assess (i) agreement among healthcare professionals on short-term prognosis, (ii) predictive accuracy of multiprofessional survival estimates, and (iii) factors affecting prognostic accuracy. A prospective observational study was conducted on patients aged ≥ 65 years with severe frailty consecutively admitted to an Acute Geriatric Unit. All participants underwent Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment and screening for palliative care needs using the NECPAL tool. Healthcare professionals provided survival estimates at 1 and 3 months through a modified surprise question. Inter-rater agreement was assessed with Fleiss' kappa. Kaplan-Meier curves were employed to compare survival across multiprofessional prognostic categories. The association between patient-related factors and prognostic accuracy was analyzed using logistic regression. For the 117 patients included (mean age: 86.4 years, 57.3% female), prognostic agreement among healthcare professionals was moderate at both 1 month (κ = 0.475) and 3 months (κ = 0.528). Multiprofessional estimates classified 39.3% of patients as having an expected survival of 3 months. During the follow-up period, 47 patients (40.2%) died, 30% of whom tested negative for NECPAL screening. Estimates differentiated patients based on short-term survival (log-rank p < 0.001) with an overall accuracy of 60.7%; positive predictive value was highest for survival beyond 3 months. Prevalent delirium was significantly associated with reduced prognostic accuracy (OR 0.38; 95% CI: 0.16-0.88). Reliable prognostic tools are needed to enhance care planning for severely frail older patients during the early stages of hospitalization. In this context, delirium assessment is crucial, as its presence significantly impacts the accuracy of short-term survival estimates, while the NECPAL tool demonstrated limited applicability.

title: Adjunctive flupentixol-melitracen for patients labelled as having refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Persistent reflux-like symptoms during proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy may reflect ongoing reflux, reflux hypersensitivity, functional heartburn, or overlapping disorders of gut-brain interaction. We assessed adjunctive flupentixol-melitracen in Chinese patients labelled as having refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease (rGERD). We reviewed controlled trials explicitly described as randomized. Quasi-randomized and non-randomized allocation were ineligible. Eight databases were searched from inception to 28 July 2026. Post-treatment arm-level data were used consistently for continuous outcomes. Random-effects models, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), exploratory subgroup and sensitivity analyses, small-study-effect tests, and GRADE assessments were performed. Twenty-nine trials (3242 participants), all conducted in China, were retained after source re-audit. Adjunctive therapy was associated with higher total clinical effectiveness (26 trials; RR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20 to 1.29; I²=0%), but this was a non-standard composite assessed largely without blinding. Anxiety (23 trials; SMD - 2.38, 95% CI - 2.93 to - 1.84; I²=97.0%; 95% PI - 5.01 to 0.24), depression (24 trials; SMD - 2.36, 95% CI - 2.86 to - 1.85; I²=96.5%; 95% PI - 4.82 to 0.11), and RDQ scores (8 trials; MD - 4.01, 95% CI - 5.27 to - 2.74; I²=98.6%; 95% PI - 7.67 to - 0.35) favored adjunctive therapy on average, but effect magnitude was highly uncertain. Eight trials sparsely reported adverse events (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.37 to 0.84); this cannot establish a protective effect or comparative safety. Small-study effects were detected for total effectiveness and the principal psychological outcomes. Certainty was very low. In Chinese trials of patients labelled as having rGERD, adjunctive flupentixol-melitracen was associated with short-term improvements in composite response and symptom scores. Extreme heterogeneity, prediction intervals crossing no effect for the psychological domains, limited objective reflux confirmation, unclear allocation concealment and blinding, small-study effects, and sparse harms reporting preclude confident estimates of benefit or safety and do not support routine use.

title: Anthropometric parameters association with the 10‑year Framingham cardiovascular disease risk score in an Iranian population: findings from the cross-sectional stage of the SHAHWAR study.
abstract: Various anthropometric components have been proposed to predict cardio-metabolic risk. This study aimed to evaluate wrist circumference (WrC) as an alternative measure to differentiate individuals with a high 10-year cardiovascular disease risk score based on the Framingham scale. We studied 1,178 adults with a mean age of 40.11 ± 7.73 who worked at a university of medical sciences in northeastern Iran. Several anthropometric indices were calculated. The 10-year risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) was estimated using the Framingham risk score. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was performed to assess the ability of anthropometric indices to predict the 10-year risk of CVD events. WrC index with the highest area under the curve (AUC = 0.836) showed significantly higher predictive power than other indices in estimating 10-year cardiovascular disease risk, followed by waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and waist circumference (WC). When the assessments were made by gender, WrC showed significantly higher predictive accuracy with 10-year cardiovascular disease risk in men compared to women, while body roundness index (BRI) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) showed equally significant predictive accuracy in predicting high 10-year cardiovascular disease risk in women. In conclusion, WrC, followed by WHR, showed the best discriminatory power for identifying adults with an elevated estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk based on the Framingham Risk Score. These findings suggest that Wrc (as a marker for body fat distribution) is more strongly associated with estimated cardiovascular risk than other anthropometric indices in this relatively young population.
